15: # Destructive Scope Violations under cli-opencode Deep-Loop Dispatch (RM-8)
16: 
17: This document records the **2026-05-04 destructive scope violation incident**, the **root cause**, and the **prevention playbook** every caller of cli-opencode (and any deep-loop dispatch wrapper that drives `opencode run`) must apply.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: Record the 2026-05-04 destructive scope violation (RM-8), explain its root cause, and provide the prevention playbook so the same uncontrolled-deletion failure cannot recur on a cli-opencode deep-loop dispatch.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: Read this before any non-interactive `opencode run` deep-loop dispatch that uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions` against a populated worktree, especially long-running `/deep:research:auto` and `/deep:review:auto` runs.
30: 
31: ### Core Principle
32: 
33: An instruction-only scope guard layered on `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is the root cause. Neither layer alone is sufficient, so prevention must add an enforced capability boundary, not more prose.
34: 
35: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. INCIDENT (2026-05-04)
40: 
41: Source-of-truth: local destructive-scope violation policy.
42: 
43: - **What ran**: `/deep:review:auto` against a phase parent across two of its phase children.
44: - **Executor**: On OpenCode 1, cli-opencode (`opencode run`) with `--model opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro --variant high --dangerously-skip-permissions --pure --dir <repo-root>`. On OpenCode 2 the effort level rides on `-m` as a `#high` suffix, the working directory moves into a `cd`, and `run` has no `--pure` ([install reference](./install-and-versions.md)).
45: - **Damage**: **44 files deleted** across the two phase children. Spec docs (`spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `checklist.md`, `decision-record.md`, `implementation-summary.md`, `description.json`, `graph-metadata.json`) **and** the `review/` packet subtrees were physically removed.
46: - **Recovery**: `git restore` from commit `7beb80769` (a pre-dispatch "bundled session sync"), a single command. **No findings lost**, but ≈30 minutes of recovery time and trust damage.
47: 
48: The deep-review skill is contractually read-only on its target spec docs. DeepSeek violated that contract.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 3. ROOT CAUSE
53: 
54: Two contributing layers, both required to enable the failure:
55: 
56: ### Layer A: unrestricted filesystem write capability
57: 
58: The YAML dispatch wrapper (`.skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-review-auto.yaml` step `if_cli_opencode`) hands the executor:
59: 
60: ```bash
61: # OpenCode 1 only
62: opencode run \
63:   --model "<provider/model>" \
64:   --agent general \
65:   --format json \
66:   --dangerously-skip-permissions \
67:   --pure \
68:   --dir "<repo-root>" \
69:   --variant <effort> \
70:   "<rendered prompt>" \
71:   </dev/null
72: ```
73: 
74: ```bash
75: # OpenCode 2
76: cd "<repo-root>" && opencode run --standalone \
77:   -m "<provider/model>#<effort>" \
78:   --agent general \
79:   --format json \
80:   "<rendered prompt>" \
81:   </dev/null
82: ```
83: 
84: On OpenCode 1, `--dangerously-skip-permissions` disables OpenCode's per-tool-call permission prompts. Combined with `--dir <repo-root>` the executor's working directory is the live worktree, and it can `rm`, `mv`, or overwrite **any** file the running user has permissions for. On OpenCode 2 there is no `--dir` flag, so the working directory is set by starting in it, and whether `run` has a permission-skip equivalent is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32 ([install reference](./install-and-versions.md)).
85: 
86: ### Layer B: instruction-only guard
87: 
88: Before the RM-8 mitigation shipped, the only safeguard against the model was a single prose line in `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/assets/prompt-pack-iteration.md.tmpl` §CONSTRAINTS:
89: 
90: > "Review target is READ-ONLY. Do not modify reviewed files."
91: 
92: That line **is not enforced anywhere**. The dispatch wrapper reads it as documentation, OpenCode does not parse it, and nothing inspects the executor's tool calls against it before they run. A confused model (DeepSeek hallucinated a cleanup step, plausibly anchored on stale spec-folder pointers it found while reading) can simply ignore the instruction, and the wrapper has no way to stop it.
93: 
94: **The combination, an instruction-only guard layered on `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, is the root cause.** Neither layer alone is sufficient to cause the damage (with permission prompts in place the model would refuse the harmless instruction-only guard, and permission-skipped dispatches with a runtime guard would survive a confused model). Both together produced the destructive event.
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 4. PREVENTION: APPLY BEFORE EVERY DEEP-LOOP DISPATCH
99: 
100: The default risk surface for cli-opencode is **any non-interactive `opencode run` invocation that uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions` against a populated worktree**, especially long-running deep-loop dispatches like `/deep:research:auto` and `/deep:review:auto`. Apply all four layers before dispatch:
101: 
102: ### Layer 1 (REQUIRED): RM-8 prompt hardening, already shipped
103: 
104: `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/assets/prompt-pack-iteration.md.tmpl` §CONSTRAINTS now includes:
105: 
106: - An **ALLOWED WRITE PATHS** list enumerating the five state-path tokens (`{state_paths_iteration_pattern}`, `{state_paths_state_log}`, `{state_paths_delta_pattern}`, `{state_paths_strategy}`, `{state_paths_findings_registry}`)
107: - A **BANNED OPERATIONS** list naming `rm`, `rm -rf`, `git rm`, `mv`, `sed -i` (including `sed -i ''`), `rmdir`, `find ... -delete`, and shell output-redirect truncate `>` against any non-allowed path
108: - A **SCOPE VIOLATION PROTOCOL**: a would-be out-of-scope mutation MUST be recorded as a `scope_violation` finding under `## SCOPE VIOLATIONS` heading instead of executed
109: 
110: This is instruction-side mitigation. It tightens the guard but does NOT remove the underlying capability. Confirm the dispatched prompt contains these strings verbatim before relying on this layer alone.
111: 
112: Policy record: local destructive-scope violation policy.
113: 
114: ### Layer 2 (STRONGLY RECOMMENDED): git worktree isolation
115: 
116: Dispatch into a `git worktree` cloned from current HEAD instead of the live worktree. Any scope violation is contained to the isolated worktree (deletable as a single directory). The main repo stays physically untouched, because on OpenCode 1 the executor's `--dir` points at the worktree path and on OpenCode 2 the dispatch starts inside the worktree with `cd` (no `--dir` on OpenCode 2 `run`, see the [install reference](./install-and-versions.md)).
117: 
118: ```bash
119: # Cut a worktree from the recovery-baseline commit
120: git worktree add --detach /Users/<you>/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/<short-name>-review HEAD
121: 
122: # Dispatch INSIDE the worktree (no --agent flag; the default agent runs when --agent is omitted)
123: # OpenCode 1 only
124: opencode run \
125:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
126:   --variant max \
127:   --format json \
128:   --dangerously-skip-permissions \
129:   --pure \
130:   --dir /Users/<you>/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/<short-name>-review \
131:   "<prompt>" \
132:   </dev/null
133: 
134: # On success: copy review/ artifacts back, prune worktree
135: # On destruction: nothing to do — main repo never saw the writes
136: git worktree remove --force /Users/<you>/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/<short-name>-review
137: ```
138: 
139: ```bash
140: # OpenCode 2
141: cd /Users/<you>/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/<short-name>-review && opencode run --standalone \
142:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
143:   --format json \
144:   "<prompt>" \
145:   </dev/null
146: ```
147: 
148: On OpenCode 2 the effort level rides on `-m` as a `#max` suffix, the working directory moves into the `cd`, and `run` has no `--pure`. Whether `run` has a permission-skip equivalent is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32 ([install reference](./install-and-versions.md)).
149: 
150: Worktree isolation is the cheapest single change that converts "deletion of N tracked files in main" into "deletion of N tracked files in throwaway worktree". For multi-phase work (the exact shape of the 2026-05-04 incident), worktrees are not optional.
151: 
152: ### Layer 3 (REQUIRED): commit-before-dispatch safety net
153: 
154: Before dispatching, commit the dispatch target's own in-flight changes on `main`, staging them by explicit path. Leave every other change in the tree alone. In a shared tree it belongs to another session, and committing it would publish work you did not write. Even with Layer 2, a commit guarantees `git restore` is a one-command recovery for the target's files if anything escapes the worktree (or if your own orchestration overwrites files in main during artifact sync-back).
155: 
156: ```bash
157: git status --short -- <relevant-paths>
158: git add <relevant-paths>
159: git diff --cached --name-only
160: git commit -m "chore(wip): snapshot in-flight work before deep-loop dispatch on <target>" -m "Recovery baseline taken before the dispatch, so its writes can be told apart."
161: ```
162: 
163: The commit hash is the recovery baseline. Surface it to the operator before dispatch. When the target has no in-flight changes there is nothing to commit, so `git rev-parse HEAD` is the baseline.
164: 
165: ### Layer 4 (FALLBACK): model selection
166: 
167: The 2026-05-04 incident was specifically observed with `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro` under `/deep:review:auto`. Until a runtime scope guard ships (see §5), the cross-phase synthesis recommendation stands: **for multi-phase deep-review work, prefer `cli-copilot` with `gpt-6-sol --reasoning-effort high`** (verify `gpt-6-sol` availability on the Copilot surface. This slug is carried over from a gpt-5.5-era Copilot-catalog check and is NOT re-verified. `opencode models openai` on OpenCode 1 does not cover Copilot. If Copilot does not expose it, pick an available Copilot model rather than silently falling back to the risky default) when available, and fall back to the flash default `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` — the default on both OpenCode versions — only with Layers 1+2+3 all in place. Memory feedback `feedback_copilot_concurrency_override.md` caps Copilot at 3 parallel dispatches. Sequence the work accordingly.
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 5. OUT OF SCOPE: RUNTIME SCOPE GUARD (future work)
172: 
173: The true RM-8 fix is a runtime scope guard:
174: 
175: - Pre-dispatch: snapshot the file tree (`git ls-tree -r HEAD` or `find ... -type f -printf '%P %s %T@\n'`)
176: - During dispatch: rely on Layers 1–3 only
177: - Post-dispatch: diff the file tree. Any modification outside the allowed-write list is reverted via `git restore` and surfaced as a `scope_violation` event
178: 
179: This requires changes to the YAML wrapper (pre/post hooks) and is a separate packet. Layer 1 + 2 + 3 are the operational ceiling until the runtime guard ships.
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## 6. QUICK CHECKLIST BEFORE DISPATCH
184: 
185: - [ ] Layer 1: rendered prompt contains literal `BANNED OPERATIONS` and `ALLOWED WRITE PATHS` strings (grep the rendered prompt before dispatch).
186: - [ ] Layer 2: on OpenCode 1 the dispatch `--dir` points at a `git worktree`, not the live working tree, and on OpenCode 2 the dispatch starts inside the worktree with `cd` (`run` has no `--dir`).
187: - [ ] Layer 3: the target's own in-flight changes committed by explicit path (staged set checked with `git diff --cached --name-only`, other sessions' changes left alone), recovery commit hash recorded.
188: - [ ] Layer 4: model+executor pairing matches risk tolerance for the target shape (single child = lower risk, phase parent with multiple children = higher risk, prefer copilot or pair with all of Layers 1–3).
189: 
190: ---
191: 
192: ## 7. RELATED MATERIAL
193: 
194: - **Incident source**: local destructive-scope violation policy
195: - **RM-8 hardening context**: local destructive-scope violation policy
196: - **Hardened prompt template**: `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/assets/prompt-pack-iteration.md.tmpl` §CONSTRAINTS
197: - **YAML dispatch surface**: `.skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-review-auto.yaml` step `if_cli_opencode`
198: - **Memory feedback**: `feedback_opencode_run_requires_dev_null_stdin.md`, `feedback_opencode_provider_fallback.md`, `feedback_cli_executor_only_when_requested.md`

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |

702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown

718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```

120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |

130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |

134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.

138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168:

172:

192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed

285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006:

1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)

1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms

1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056:

17: # OpenCode CLI - Install and Version Layouts
18: 
19: How to put OpenCode 2.1.4 on a machine, optionally alongside OpenCode 1.19.4 as a fallback, and how to tell which version a name runs.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: This reference is the skill's install guidance. OpenCode 2 is the version this repository expects and recommends; OpenCode 1 is a backwards-compatible fallback kept only because not every user has updated yet. A dispatch needs a known binary, and the two supported majors are separate npm packages that both claim the name `opencode`. What follows is the layouts that work, the helper that builds them, and the facts that decide which version answers a bare `opencode`.
28: 
29: ### Claim Labels
30: 
31: Claims in the prose carry one of three labels. The layout table in section 3 summarises the sections below it, whose claims are labelled there.
32: 
33: | Label | Meaning |
34: |-------|---------|
35: | `[confirmed]` | Observed on this machine on 2026-10-18 with the command named in the sentence. |
36: | `[documented]` | Stated by a named source: the official v2 docs at https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/, the launcher comment in `~/.local/bin/opencode1`, the CLI's own `--help` output, or the npm registry. |
37: | `[unknown]` | Not probed. Treat it as open and do not plan around it. |
38: 
39: ### The Fact Behind Every Collision
40: 
41: Both majors ship a binary named `opencode` [confirmed: `npm view opencode-ai bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe' }` and `npm view @opencode/cli bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe', opencode2: 'bin/opencode.exe' }`]. One prefix therefore cannot hold both versions under that name. v2 is the expected version, so it keeps the name `opencode`, and v1 is the one that moves: side by side it answers only to the `opencode1` launcher. The second v2 name, `opencode2`, is retired in that layout.
42: 
43: ### When to Use
44: 
45: - Installing OpenCode 2.1.4, alone or side by side with the `opencode1` launcher for v1
46: - Installing OpenCode 1.19.4 alone or side by side, the fallback path for users who have not updated
47: - Deciding whether Homebrew, mise or a second npm prefix is the right channel
48: - Working out why a bare `opencode` runs the version you did not expect
49: 
50: ### Key Sources
51: 
52: | Source | What it gives you |
53: |--------|-------------------|
54: | `~/.local/bin/opencode1` | The v1 launcher that keeps the two databases apart |
55: | https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/ | The official v2 install channels and the v2 platform docs |
56: | `../scripts/opencode-setup.sh` | The helper that builds any of the three layouts |
57: | `./cli-reference.md` | Subcommands, `run` flags and the version-drift section |
58: 
59: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in this reference.
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: ## 2. PREREQUISITES
64: 
65: ### Tooling
66: 
67: - Node.js and npm for every npm layout. The npm on this machine is `/opt/homebrew/bin/npm` 11.19.1 [confirmed: `command -v npm` and `npm -v`].
68: - A POSIX shell for the launcher, which is `/bin/sh` [confirmed: the launcher's shebang].
69: - macOS or Linux. The npm path is cross-platform. The Homebrew channels are not.
70: 
71: ### Pinned Targets
72: 
73: | Version | Package | Pin | Channel `latest` |
74: |---------|---------|-----|------------------|
75: | v2 (recommended) | `@opencode/cli` | `2.1.4` | `2.1.4` |
76: | v1 (fallback) | `opencode-ai` | `1.19.4` | `1.19.4` |
77: 
78: Each pin is its package's current `latest` [confirmed: `npm view @opencode/cli dist-tags` and `npm view opencode-ai dist-tags`, read 2026-10-24]. The v1 package was not moved to 2.x, so a v1 package update cannot drift a v1 install into v2 [confirmed: `opencode-ai`'s `latest` dist-tag is 1.19.4].
79: 
80: ### Read First
81: 
82: The name collision in "The Fact Behind Every Collision" decides almost every choice below. If you are adding a second version to a machine that already has one, read section 3 before you run any install command.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 3. INSTALLATION
87: 
88: ### The Three Layouts
89: 
90: Read the warning in a layout's own section before you run its command. The v2 layouts come first because OpenCode 2 is the recommended target; the v1-only layout is the fallback for users who have not updated. Each row takes the `opencode` name: the v2 rows orphan or shadow an existing v1 install, and the v1 row collides with a v2 `opencode` already on `PATH`.
91: 
92: | Setup | Channel | Command | `opencode` resolves to | Data file |
93: |-------|---------|---------|------------------------|-----------|
94: | v2 only (recommended) | npm, standard prefix | `npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.1.4` | v2 | `opencode.db`, unless `OPENCODE_DB` says otherwise |
95: | v2 only (recommended) | Homebrew | `brew install opencode` | v2 | `opencode.db` |
96: | both (recommended) | npm, two prefixes | both npm commands below, plus the v2 links and the `opencode1` launcher | v2 | `opencode.db` for v2, `opencode-v1.db` for v1 |
97: | v1 only (fallback) | npm | `npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" opencode-ai@1.19.4` | v1 | `opencode.db` |
98: 
99: The two-prefix npm layout is the only verified way to hold both versions on one machine [documented: the npm registry]. It needs the `opencode1` launcher, which gives v1 a name of its own and a database of its own.
100: 
101: ### Layout 1: v2 Only (Recommended)
102: 
103: Two things to settle first.
104: 
105: 1. `npm install -g @opencode/cli` to the standard prefix takes the `opencode` name. If a v1 `opencode` already resolves, this orphans the v1 install. Use the side-by-side layout instead [documented: the npm registry].
106: 2. If `$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` exists from an earlier v1 install, v2 adopts that database and migrates it in place [confirmed: on 2026-10-24 the first v2.1.4 run on this machine added a `session_v2` table to `opencode.db` holding all 1,339 v1 sessions]. Copy the file aside or set `OPENCODE_DB` before the first run if v1 must keep reading it. The helper warns about this and never moves a file.
107: 
108: ```bash
109: npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.1.4
110: opencode --version    # opencode v2.1.4
111: ```
112: 
113: ### Layout 2: Side by Side (Recommended for One Machine)
114: 
115: v2 takes the name `opencode` and v1 moves to `opencode1`; no `opencode2` is on `PATH`. The working layout is four artifacts [confirmed: this is the state of this machine on 2026-10-24].
116: 
117: 1. v1 in the default npm prefix, `~/.local/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai`. Its npm install writes `~/.local/bin/opencode`, and the next step takes that name back.
118: 2. v2 in a second prefix, `~/.local/opencode-v2`. The install lands two names there, `opencode` and `opencode2`, both pointing at one binary [confirmed: `~/.local/opencode-v2/bin/` holds both symlinks to `../lib/node_modules/@opencode/cli/bin/opencode.exe`]. That prefix bin is not on `PATH`.
119: 3. `~/.local/bin/opencode`, a symlink to `../opencode-v2/lib/node_modules/@opencode/cli/bin/opencode.exe`. A bare `opencode` runs v2 against the default `opencode.db`.
120: 4. The launcher at `~/.local/bin/opencode1`, a `/bin/sh` script that sets `OPENCODE_DB=opencode-v1.db` and `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1` and execs the v1 binary.
121: 
122: ```bash
123: npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" opencode-ai@1.19.4
124: npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local/opencode-v2" @opencode/cli@2.1.4
125: ln -sfn ../opencode-v2/lib/node_modules/@opencode/cli/bin/opencode.exe "$HOME/.local/bin/opencode"
126: # then write ~/.local/bin/opencode1 (the text is in section 4)
127: ```
128: 
129: Order matters: the link comes after the v1 install, because that install writes the name `opencode`. Any later reinstall of `opencode-ai` into `~/.local` takes the name back. v1's own auto-update does exactly that [confirmed: on 2026-10-24 v1 updated itself to 1.19.4 and `~/.local/bin/opencode` pointed at v1 again], which is why the launcher turns auto-update off. Run `opencode-setup.sh check` after any v1 npm operation, and rerun `both` if `opencode` reports v1.
130: 
131: Before the first v2 run on a machine that already has v1 history, copy `opencode.db` for v1, because v2 migrates it in place:
132: 
133: ```bash
134: sqlite3 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db" ".backup '$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode-v1.db'"
135: ```
136: 
137: ### Layout 3: v1 Only (Fallback)
138: 
139: Use this only when you have not moved to OpenCode 2 yet. Before you install, check that no `opencode` on `PATH` already resolves to v2. If one does, stop and resolve the collision by hand. Do not overwrite it.
140: 
141: ```bash
142: npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" opencode-ai@1.19.4
143: "$HOME/.local/bin/opencode" --version    # 1.19.4
144: ```
145: 
146: No launcher is needed, because with only v1 present there is nothing to disambiguate. The v1 channel still moves by patch releases, so install with the explicit `@1.19.4` pin to stay on the verified version [confirmed: `opencode-ai`'s `latest` dist-tag is 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24]. Because OpenCode 1 support is temporary, this is a holding position rather than a target: move to v2, or to the side-by-side layout, when you can.
147: 
148: ### The Setup Helper
149: 
150: `../scripts/opencode-setup.sh <v2|both|v1|check>` builds any of the three layouts [documented: the helper contract].
151: 
152: | Mode | What it does |
153: |------|--------------|
154: | `v2` (recommended) | Installs v2 to the standard prefix. Refuses when a v1 `opencode` already resolves and prints the `both` hint. |
155: | `both` (recommended) | Installs v1 and v2 into the two prefixes, links `opencode` to v2, retires `opencode2`, writes the `opencode1` launcher last, then reports both names. An `opencode2` link into the v2 prefix is removed; any other file at `opencode` or `opencode2` is moved aside to `<name>.pre-v2-default`, never deleted. |
156: | `v1` (fallback) | Installs v1 only, for users who have not updated. Refuses when a v2 `opencode` already resolves and prints the `both` hint. |
157: | `check` | Changes nothing. Reports the resolved path and the version for each name. |
158: 
159: Every mode is idempotent, and every step prints its rollback line. The helper never runs a rollback, an uninstall or an upgrade, and it changes no data file: when `opencode.db` exists and `opencode-v1.db` does not, `both` prints the copy command above instead of running it. It writes the links and the launcher only after both npm installs succeed. If the second npm install fails, the first stays installed and nothing else is written. Rerunning `both` completes the layout.
160: 
161: `check` reads the binaries from `$HOME` rather than from the caller's `PATH`, so it reports the layout even when the two disagree [documented: the helper contract].
162: 
163: ### Official v2 Channels
164: 
165: The official v2 channels as of 2026-10-18 [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/].
166: 
167: The v2 binary is named `opencode`, the same as v1's [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/], so none of these channels solves side-by-side on its own. The `opencode1` launcher is still required.
168: 
169: - `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash`
170: - `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2`
171: - `npm install -g @opencode/cli`
172: - bun, pnpm, yarn and Vite+ install paths
173: - AUR package `opencode-beta`
174: - `mise use -g opencode`. mise 2026.10.9 and later install OpenCode 2 under the name `opencode`, while older mise versions install OpenCode 1 [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/]. A mise upgrade alone can therefore move a user from v1 to v2 with no explicit choice, so pin the version when you need to stay on v1.
175: 
176: ### Homebrew Is v2-Only and Exclusive
177: 
178: `brew install opencode` installs a v2 `opencode` on the default `PATH` [confirmed: `brew info --json=v2 opencode` reports stable `2.0.32`, and the formula tracks the v2 repository].
179: 
180: There is no `opencode@1` formula and no versioned formula at all [confirmed: `versioned_formulae` is an empty list]. Homebrew therefore cannot supply the v1 leg of a side-by-side layout, and a Homebrew v2 collides with an npm v1 on the `opencode` name. One of the two becomes invisible depending on `PATH` order. Treat Homebrew as a v2-only, exclusive channel. Use it when you want only v2, and use the two-prefix npm layout when you want both.
181: 
182: ---
183: 
184: ## 4. CONFIGURATION
185: 
186: ### The Launcher
187: 
188: The launcher carries the isolation, not the packages. Its text, verbatim [confirmed: this is the file at `~/.local/bin/opencode1` on this machine, byte-identical to what the helper writes].
189: 
190: ```sh
191: #!/bin/sh
192: # OpenCode 1 fallback. OpenCode 2 owns opencode.db and migrates it in place,
193: # so v1 keeps its own copy. A relative OPENCODE_DB resolves under the shared data directory.
194: # An auto-update reinstalls the v1 package, which takes the opencode name back from v2.
195: : "${OPENCODE_DB:=opencode-v1.db}"
196: : "${OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE:=1}"
197: export OPENCODE_DB OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE
198: exec "$HOME/.local/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/opencode.exe" "$@"
199: ```
200: 
201: ### Why OPENCODE_DB Is Set
202: 
203: Both versions open `opencode.db` by default, and v2 migrates it in place [confirmed: see Layout 1]. v2 is the expected version, so it keeps the default file and v1 moves to `opencode-v1.db`. Both versions honour `OPENCODE_DB`, and a relative value resolves under the shared data directory, so `opencode-v1.db` lands beside `opencode.db` rather than in the current working directory [confirmed: on 2026-10-24 two `opencode1 run` calls added two sessions to `opencode-v1.db`, two v2 runs added two to `opencode.db`, and `opencode-v1.db` has no `session_v2` table].
204: 
205: `~/.local/share/opencode/` holds four databases on this machine [confirmed]: `opencode.db` (v2), `opencode-v1.db` (v1), `opencode-v2.db`, which holds the v2 sessions from the earlier layout and is no longer opened by either name, and `opencode-next.db`, residue from a v2 preview build. v2 imports `opencode-next.db` on its first run on a database; nothing imports `opencode-v2.db` [documented: the v2 binary's migration code reads `opencode-next.db` by name].
206: 
207: The `: "${OPENCODE_DB:=opencode-v1.db}"` form sets the variable only when it is unset or empty, so a caller can still override it for one run:
208: 
209: ```bash
210: OPENCODE_DB=/tmp/probe.db opencode1 run ...
211: ```
212: 
213: ### The Config Directory Is Shared
214: 
215: Both versions read `~/.config/opencode`, and there is no per-version config directory [confirmed: the directory holds one `opencode.jsonc`, one `plugins/` tree and one `service.json`, with no version-suffixed sibling]. A key written for one version is live on the other immediately [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/, which puts the global config at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`]. Nothing isolates them.
216: 
217: That has two consequences you cannot design around:
218: 
219: - A config key only one version understands can break the other.
220: - `~/.config/opencode` is never cleanup after uninstalling one version.
221: 
222: ### How cli-opencode Picks a Binary
223: 
224: The runtime resolves the executor in this order [documented: the cli-opencode dispatch contract].
225: 
226: 1. `$OPENCODE_BIN`, when set.
227: 2. Otherwise take `opencode2` from anywhere on `PATH`.
228: 3. Only when no `opencode2` exists anywhere on `PATH`, fall back to the first `opencode`.
229: 
230: Both halves are worth knowing. With no `OPENCODE_BIN`, the side-by-side layout has no `opencode2`, so the pick on this machine is `~/.local/bin/opencode` and a bare dispatch runs v2 [confirmed]. Reaching v1 takes `OPENCODE_BIN=opencode1` [confirmed: `opencode1 --version` reports a 1.x version]. A v2-only layout that installs only `opencode` reaches v2 through step 3, and a v1-only machine reaches v1 the same way.
231: 
232: The rule is deliberately v2-first. OpenCode 2 is the version the repository expects and recommends; OpenCode 1 is kept only as a fallback for machines that have not updated. Resolution therefore never lets an earlier `opencode` on `PATH` beat an `opencode2` that exists later, and a `check` that reports `1.19.4` for a bare `opencode` is reporting the fallback.
233: 
234: ### Run Flags Differ Between Versions
235: 
236: The two versions do not take the same `run` flags, so a shared argv does not exist.
237: 
238: | Concern | v2 2.0.32 (recommended) | v1 1.19.3 (fallback) |
239: |---------|-------------------------|------------------------|
240: | Working directory | No flag. The spawn directory carries it. | `--dir <path>` |
241: | Positional arguments | message text only, so every positional is a message | message text |
242: | Variant | rides on the model id, `-m provider/model#variant` | `--variant max` |
243: | Permission bypass | `--auto` | `--auto`, with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` as a hidden alias |
244: | Private server | `--standalone` for a dispatch that should not use the background service | not needed |
245: 
246: The v2 `run` surface on this machine is `--standalone`, `--server`, `--continue`, `--session`, `--fork`, `--model`, `--agent`, `--format`, `--file`, `--title`, `--thinking` and `--auto`, and its help lists the arguments as `message...` [confirmed: `run --help` on 2.0.32]. The v1 `run` surface adds `--dir` and `--variant`, which v2 does not have [confirmed: `run --help` on 1.19.3].
247: 
248: The `--dangerously-skip-permissions` alias is hidden from help and appears only in v1's bundled option table, where it is registered as a hidden alias of `--auto` [documented: the v1 option table]. Pass `--auto` on both versions unless a caller already pins the v1 argv.
249: 
250: ### Providers Are Per Version
251: 
252: The two versions list different providers, so a model id that works on one can be missing on the other [confirmed: the two lists below, read on this machine on 2026-10-18].
253: 
254: | Command | Roster-relevant providers listed |
255: |---------|----------------------------------|
256: | `opencode models --standalone` (2.0.32, recommended) | llmgateway-providers, llmgateway, opencode |
257: | `opencode models` (1.19.3, fallback) | llmgateway-providers, llmgateway, opencode-go, openai, opencode, minimax |
258: 
259: A listing also shows any provider whose credential is still in the local auth store, including one that is off the roster. Such a provider is not a dispatch target.
260: 
261: v2 2.0.32 lists `llmgateway`, `llmgateway-providers` and `opencode`; v1 1.19.3 lists `opencode-go`, `openai` and `minimax`, which v2 2.0.32 does not [confirmed: both versions' model listings on 2026-10-18, and `opencode models --standalone` on 2026-10-20, which lists the same v2 provider prefixes]. The former OpenCode 1 default model, `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, names the `opencode-go` provider, which v2 does not list [confirmed: `opencode models` on 1.19.3], so the default on both versions is `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, which v2 does list.
262: 
263: Check the provider on the version you are about to dispatch. For a v2 run, list with `opencode models --standalone` and look for the `<provider>/` prefix: v2 `models` takes no provider argument, and without `--standalone` it asks the shared background service. For a v1 run, use `opencode1 models` side by side, or `opencode models` on a v1-only machine. Whether credentials added on one version reach the other was not probed [unknown].
264: 
265: ---
266: 
267: ## 5. VERIFICATION
268: 
269: ### Detect by Output Shape
270: 
271: ```bash
272: opencode --version    # opencode v2.1.4   -> v2 (recommended)
273: opencode1 --version   # 1.19.4            -> v1 (fallback)
274: ```
275: 
276: Both lines are observed output on this machine on 2026-10-24 [confirmed], and both match the pins.
277: 
278: Do not detect by name. A v1-only machine answers v1 to `opencode`, every other layout answers v2 to it, and only the side-by-side layout has `opencode1` [documented: the npm registry, where `@opencode/cli` declares both `opencode` and `opencode2`, so a plain v2 install also answers to `opencode2`]. Classify by what the binary prints:
279: 
280: - an `opencode v2.0.32` shape, a word before the number, is v2
281: - a bare `1.19.3` shape, digits and dots only, is v1
282: 
283: Anchor the pattern. A string like `1.19.3garbage` must not pass as v1, and the committed guard rejects it [documented: the guard's anchored pattern].
284: 
285: ### What `--version` Proves
286: 
287: `--version` proves which version a name runs. That is all it proves.
288: 
289: It does not prove that plugins load, that the config parses, that a provider is authenticated or that a dispatch will succeed. Those legs stay [unknown]. A pair that reports `1.19.3` and `opencode v2.0.32` is installed, not verified. Say "reports its version" rather than "works" until a real run has loaded a plugin on both.
290: 
291: ### What a Probe Writes
292: 
293: A v2 `--version` call is not read-only. The binary appends a `cli starting` line to `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` on every invocation, `--version` included, and `--log-level none` does not stop it, in either argument order. v1 `--version` writes nothing [confirmed: repeated probes on this machine, 2026-10-18].
294: 
295: The setup helper points `XDG_DATA_HOME` at a temporary folder for each `--version` probe and removes the folder on exit, so its probes write nothing under HOME [confirmed: a v2 probe with that variable set wrote its log line in the temporary folder, and the HOME log was unchanged, 2026-10-18]. A `--version` you run by hand still writes the log line.
296: 
297: ### Verify a Layout by Hand
298: 
299: ```bash
300: "$HOME/.local/bin/opencode" --version    # v2
301: "$HOME/.local/bin/opencode1" --version   # v1
302: ls -1 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode"/*.db
303: ```
304: 
305: ### The `check` Mode
306: 
307: `../scripts/opencode-setup.sh check` runs all of the above and changes nothing. It prints the resolved path and the reported version for `opencode`, `opencode1` and any leftover `opencode2`, which version the bare word `opencode` runs, and the database files present [documented: the helper contract].
308: 
309: ---
310: 
311: ## 6. UPGRADE
312: 
313: ### A Plain v1 Upgrade Cannot Reach 2.x
314: 
315: `opencode upgrade` with no target resolves against the `opencode-ai` channel, whose `latest` is 1.19.4, the pinned version [confirmed: `opencode upgrade --help` on 1.19.3 and the npm dist-tags on 2026-10-24]. The channel still moves by patch releases, which is why the launcher turns auto-update off and the setup helper installs the explicit pin. Nothing you do to keep v1 current can move it to 2.x except the flag below.
316: 
317: ### Never Run `opencode upgrade --major`
318: 
319: **Stop. Read the flag's own help text before you type it.**
320: 
321: ```
322: --major       upgrade to OpenCode 2 and remove OpenCode 1   [boolean]
323: ```
324: 
325: That is the complete description on 1.19.3 [confirmed]. The removal is in the flag's contract, not an implementation detail. On a side-by-side machine, `--major` migrates v1 to v2 and deletes the v1 install, which destroys the layout you built. It is a migration, never an upgrade. Do not put it in a script, a recipe or a troubleshooting step.
326: 
327: Whether it prompts for confirmation before it acts was not probed [unknown].
328: 
329: ### `upgrade --method` Is Version-Specific
330: 
331: | Method | v2 2.0.32 (recommended) | v1 1.19.3 (fallback) |
332: |--------|-------------------------|------------------------|
333: | curl, npm, pnpm, bun, brew | yes | yes |
334: | choco, scoop | no | yes |
335: | yarn, vp, winget | yes | no |
336: 
337: Both columns are read from the `--help` output on this machine [confirmed]. A shared recipe must not pass `--method`. Let each version pick its own, or build the flag per version.
338: 
339: Only the shared five are usable here, because yarn, vp and winget are absent from this machine [confirmed: `command -v`], and only npm and curl are plausible in a script.
340: 
341: ### `--log-level` Is Version-Specific Too
342: 
343: v1 accepts `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN` and `ERROR`, uppercase only [confirmed: v1 help]. v2 accepts `all`, `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `warning`, `error`, `fatal` and `none`, lowercase [confirmed: v2 help]. A shared script that passes `--log-level WARN` to v2 fails, and `--log-level warn` to v1 fails. Omit the flag, or build it per version.
344: 
345: ---
346: 
347: ## 7. UNINSTALLATION
348: 
349: ### Rollback Lines
350: 
351: The helper prints these and never runs them. Run them by hand, one layout at a time.
352: 
353: ```bash
354: # v2 leg
355: "$HOME/.local/opencode-v2/bin/opencode" uninstall --dry-run    # inspect first
356: "$HOME/.local/opencode-v2/bin/opencode" uninstall --force      # documented as keeping session data, config, state
357: npm uninstall -g --prefix "$HOME/.local/opencode-v2" @opencode/cli   # when the prefix itself goes
358: 
359: # v1 leg (fallback)
360: npm uninstall -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" opencode-ai
361: 
362: # after the v2 leg: remove ~/.local/bin/opencode, now a dangling link
363: # after the v1 leg: remove ~/.local/bin/opencode1, now a launcher with no binary
364: # after either: DO NOT delete ~/.config/opencode
365: ```
366: 
367: ### Order Matters
368: 
369: Each leg leaves names behind. Removing v2 leaves `opencode` pointing at a missing binary, and removing v1 leaves `opencode1` execing one [documented: the links' targets and the launcher's exec line]. The leftovers are harmless but confusing, and the next `check` reports names that no longer work. Whether `npm uninstall` of `opencode-ai` also removes the `opencode` link, which now points into the v2 prefix, was not probed [unknown]. Run `check` afterwards.
370: 
371: ### What v2's Uninstall Keeps
372: 
373: `opencode uninstall` is described as `Uninstall OpenCode, keeping session data, configuration, and state`, and it offers `--dry-run` to print the manifest and `--force` to skip confirmation [confirmed: `uninstall --help` on 2.0.32]. Run `--dry-run` first, read it, then `--force`.
374: 
375: On the v1 side, `npm uninstall -g --prefix ~/.local opencode-ai` removes the package. The session data in `~/.local/share/opencode/` is untouched by the npm operation [documented: the npm registry].
376: 
377: Whether the v2 background service outlives the uninstall was not probed [unknown]. Check the process list after a rollback rather than assuming either way.
378: 
379: ### Never Delete the Config Directory
380: 
381: `~/.config/opencode` is shared by both versions [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/, which puts the global config at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`]. Never delete it as post-uninstall cleanup. Both versions read it, so removing it breaks whichever one remains.
382: 
383: ---
384: 
385: ## 8. TROUBLESHOOTING
386: 
387: ### Symptoms
388: 
389: | Symptom | Cause | Fix |
390: |---------|-------|-----|
391: | `opencode --version` prints `1.19.4` on a side-by-side machine | A v1 npm operation or a v1 auto-update took the `opencode` name back | Rerun `opencode-setup.sh both`, which relinks `opencode` to v2 |
392: | A v1 run opens the database v2 migrated | `OPENCODE_DB` is unset and the run bypassed the `opencode1` launcher | Run `opencode1` from `~/.local/bin`, or set `OPENCODE_DB=opencode-v1.db` yourself |
393: | A dispatch picks a version you did not expect | `$OPENCODE_BIN` is set; otherwise the first `opencode2` anywhere on `PATH` wins, and the first `opencode` is the fallback only when no `opencode2` exists | Read the resolved path, then pin `$OPENCODE_BIN` for the run |
394: | `provider/model not found` on v2 for a model that works on v1 | The provider lists differ per version | Confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix before the dispatch |
395: | `opencode1` prints `No such file or directory` and exits 126 [confirmed: a launcher whose target is missing, run on this machine] | The v1 package was uninstalled or moved | Reinstall v1, or remove the launcher |
396: | `npm` aborts with a dyld `Library not loaded` error | The node that npm runs cannot start [confirmed: Homebrew node 26.11.1 on this machine] | Put a working node earlier on `PATH` |
397: 
398: ### Gaps That No Recipe Closes
399: 
400: These constraints survive every layout. Plan around them rather than trying to fix them.
401: 
402: 1. **Homebrew cannot coexist with a v1 install.** The formula is v2-only, no versioned formula exists, and both binaries are named `opencode`.
403: 2. **`upgrade --major` is a migration that removes v1.** No recipe makes it safe on a side-by-side machine.
404: 3. **The config directory is shared.** One `~/.config/opencode` serves both versions, and a key written for one is live on the other immediately. No isolation exists to document.
405: 4. **The default database is shared.** Both versions open `opencode.db` unless `OPENCODE_DB` is set, and v2 migrates it. The `opencode1` launcher is the only thing keeping v1 off the migrated file.
406: 5. **v2's background service has no v1 analogue [confirmed: `opencode --help` lists a `service` group that `opencode --help` does not, and one service process serves the v2 clients on this machine].** Whether it outlives an uninstall was not probed [unknown].
407: 6. **`upgrade --method` and `--log-level` are version-specific.** A shared recipe must omit both.
408: 7. **bun and pnpm two-prefix behaviour is unestablished.** Only npm was verified for the two-prefix layout. Treat the other managers as single-version rather than implying parity.
409: 
410: ### Open Questions
411: 
412: | Question | Status |
413: |----------|--------|
414: | Does the v2 service outlive `opencode uninstall`? | [unknown] Not probed. |
415: | Do `bun add -g` and `pnpm add -g` support the two-prefix layout? | [unknown] Not probed. |
416: | Does `upgrade --major` prompt before it acts? | [unknown] Not probed. |
417: | Do the `@opencode/cli` install scripts start a service? | [unknown] Not probed. |
418: 
419: ---
420: 
421: ## 9. RELATED RESOURCES
422: 
423: - [`./cli-reference.md`](./cli-reference.md) for the subcommand map, the `run` flag surface and the version-drift section
424: - [`./providers-and-models.md`](./providers-and-models.md) for the provider roster and the per-provider variant map
425: - [`../scripts/opencode-setup.sh`](../scripts/opencode-setup.sh) for the `v2`, `both`, `v1` and `check` modes
426: - https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/ for the official v2 channels and the v2 platform documentation
