16: 
17: # OpenCode CLI - Install and Version Layouts
18: 
19: How to put OpenCode 2.1.4 on a machine, optionally alongside OpenCode 1.19.4 as a fallback, and how to tell which version a name runs.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: This reference is the skill's install guidance. OpenCode 2 is the version this repository expects and recommends; OpenCode 1 is a backwards-compatible fallback kept only because not every user has updated yet. A dispatch needs a known binary, and the two supported majors are separate npm packages that both claim the name `opencode`. What follows is the layouts that work, the helper that builds them, and the facts that decide which version answers a bare `opencode`.
28: 
29: ### Claim Labels
30: 
31: Claims in the prose carry one of three labels. The layout table in section 3 summarises the sections below it, whose claims are labelled there.
32: 
33: | Label | Meaning |
34: |-------|---------|
35: | `[confirmed]` | Observed on this machine on 2026-10-18 with the command named in the sentence. |
36: | `[documented]` | Stated by a named source: the official v2 docs at https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/, the launcher comment in `~/.local/bin/opencode1`, the CLI's own `--help` output, or the npm registry. |
37: | `[unknown]` | Not probed. Treat it as open and do not plan around it. |
38: 
39: ### The Fact Behind Every Collision
40: 
41: Both majors ship a binary named `opencode` [confirmed: `npm view opencode-ai bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe' }` and `npm view @opencode/cli bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe', opencode2: 'bin/opencode.exe' }`]. One prefix therefore cannot hold both versions under that name. v2 is the expected version, so it keeps the name `opencode`, and v1 is the one that moves: side by side it answers only to the `opencode1` launcher. The second v2 name, `opencode2`, is retired in that layout.
42: 
43: ### When to Use
44: 
45: - Installing OpenCode 2.1.4, alone or side by side with the `opencode1` launcher for v1
46: - Installing OpenCode 1.19.4 alone or side by side, the fallback path for users who have not updated
47: - Deciding whether Homebrew, mise or a second npm prefix is the right channel
48: - Working out why a bare `opencode` runs the version you did not expect
49: 
50: ### Key Sources
51: 
52: | Source | What it gives you |
53: |--------|-------------------|
54: | `~/.local/bin/opencode1` | The v1 launcher that keeps the two databases apart |
55: | https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/ | The official v2 install channels and the v2 platform docs |
56: | `../scripts/opencode-setup.sh` | The helper that builds any of the three layouts |
57: | `./cli-reference.md` | Subcommands, `run` flags and the version-drift section |
58: 
59: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in this reference.
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: ## 2. PREREQUISITES
64: 
65: ### Tooling
66: 
67: - Node.js and npm for every npm layout. The npm on this machine is `/opt/homebrew/bin/npm` 11.19.1 [confirmed: `command -v npm` and `npm -v`].
68: - A POSIX shell for the launcher, which is `/bin/sh` [confirmed: the launcher's shebang].
69: - macOS or Linux. The npm path is cross-platform. The Homebrew channels are not.
70: 
71: ### Pinned Targets
72: 
73: | Version | Package | Pin | Channel `latest` |
74: |---------|---------|-----|------------------|
75: | v2 (recommended) | `@opencode/cli` | `2.1.4` | `2.1.4` |
76: | v1 (fallback) | `opencode-ai` | `1.19.4` | `1.19.4` |
77: 
78: Each pin is its package's current `latest` [confirmed: `npm view @opencode/cli dist-tags` and `npm view opencode-ai dist-tags`, read 2026-10-24]. The v1 package was not moved to 2.x, so a v1 package update cannot drift a v1 install into v2 [confirmed: `opencode-ai`'s `latest` dist-tag is 1.19.4].
79: 
80: ### Read First
81: 
82: The name collision in "The Fact Behind Every Collision" decides almost every choice below. If you are adding a second version to a machine that already has one, read section 3 before you run any install command.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 3. INSTALLATION
87: 
88: ### The Three Layouts
89: 
90: Read the warning in a layout's own section before you run its command. The v2 layouts come first because OpenCode 2 is the recommended target; the v1-only layout is the fallback for users who have not updated. Each row takes the `opencode` name: the v2 rows orphan or shadow an existing v1 install, and the v1 row collides with a v2 `opencode` already on `PATH`.
91: 
92: | Setup | Channel | Command | `opencode` resolves to | Data file |
93: |-------|---------|---------|------------------------|-----------|
94: | v2 only (recommended) | npm, standard prefix | `npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.1.4` | v2 | `opencode.db`, unless `OPENCODE_DB` says otherwise |
95: | v2 only (recommended) | Homebrew | `brew install opencode` | v2 | `opencode.db` |
96: | both (recommended) | npm, two prefixes | both npm commands below, plus the v2 links and the `opencode1` launcher | v2 | `opencode.db` for v2, `opencode-v1.db` for v1 |
97: | v1 only (fallback) | npm | `npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" opencode-ai@1.19.4` | v1 | `opencode.db` |
98: 
99: The two-prefix npm layout is the only verified way to hold both versions on one machine [documented: the npm registry]. It needs the `opencode1` launcher, which gives v1 a name of its own and a database of its own.
100: 
101: ### Layout 1: v2 Only (Recommended)
102: 
103: Two things to settle first.
104: 
105: 1. `npm install -g @opencode/cli` to the standard prefix takes the `opencode` name. If a v1 `opencode` already resolves, this orphans the v1 install. Use the side-by-side layout instead [documented: the npm registry].
106: 2. If `$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` exists from an earlier v1 install, v2 adopts that database and migrates it in place [confirmed: on 2026-10-24 the first v2.1.4 run on this machine added a `session_v2` table to `opencode.db` holding all 1,339 v1 sessions]. Copy the file aside or set `OPENCODE_DB` before the first run if v1 must keep reading it. The helper warns about this and never moves a file.
107: 
108: ```bash
109: npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.1.4
110: opencode --version    # opencode v2.1.4
111: ```
112: 
113: ### Layout 2: Side by Side (Recommended for One Machine)
114: 
115: v2 takes the name `opencode` and v1 moves to `opencode1`; no `opencode2` is on `PATH`. The working layout is four artifacts [confirmed: this is the state of this machine on 2026-10-24].
116: 
117: 1. v1 in the default npm prefix, `~/.local/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai`. Its npm install writes `~/.local/bin/opencode`, and the next step takes that name back.
118: 2. v2 in a second prefix, `~/.local/opencode-v2`. The install lands two names there, `opencode` and `opencode2`, both pointing at one binary [confirmed: `~/.local/opencode-v2/bin/` holds both symlinks to `../lib/node_modules/@opencode/cli/bin/opencode.exe`]. That prefix bin is not on `PATH`.
119: 3. `~/.local/bin/opencode`, a symlink to `../opencode-v2/lib/node_modules/@opencode/cli/bin/opencode.exe`. A bare `opencode` runs v2 against the default `opencode.db`.
120: 4. The launcher at `~/.local/bin/opencode1`, a `/bin/sh` script that sets `OPENCODE_DB=opencode-v1.db` and `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1` and execs the v1 binary.
121: 
122: ```bash
123: npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" opencode-ai@1.19.4
124: npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local/opencode-v2" @opencode/cli@2.1.4
125: ln -sfn ../opencode-v2/lib/node_modules/@opencode/cli/bin/opencode.exe "$HOME/.local/bin/opencode"
126: # then write ~/.local/bin/opencode1 (the text is in section 4)
127: ```
128: 
129: Order matters: the link comes after the v1 install, because that install writes the name `opencode`. Any later reinstall of `opencode-ai` into `~/.local` takes the name back. v1's own auto-update does exactly that [confirmed: on 2026-10-24 v1 updated itself to 1.19.4 and `~/.local/bin/opencode` pointed at v1 again], which is why the launcher turns auto-update off. Run `opencode-setup.sh check` after any v1 npm operation, and rerun `both` if `opencode` reports v1.
130: 
131: Before the first v2 run on a machine that already has v1 history, copy `opencode.db` for v1, because v2 migrates it in place:
132: 
133: ```bash
134: sqlite3 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db" ".backup '$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode-v1.db'"
135: ```
136: 
137: ### Layout 3: v1 Only (Fallback)
138: 
139: Use this only when you have not moved to OpenCode 2 yet. Before you install, check that no `opencode` on `PATH` already resolves to v2. If one does, stop and resolve the collision by hand. Do not overwrite it.
140: 
141: ```bash
142: npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" opencode-ai@1.19.4
143: "$HOME/.local/bin/opencode" --version    # 1.19.4
144: ```
145: 
146: No launcher is needed, because with only v1 present there is nothing to disambiguate. The v1 channel still moves by patch releases, so install with the explicit `@1.19.4` pin to stay on the verified version [confirmed: `opencode-ai`'s `latest` dist-tag is 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24]. Because OpenCode 1 support is temporary, this is a holding position rather than a target: move to v2, or to the side-by-side layout, when you can.
147: 
148: ### The Setup Helper
149: 
150: `../scripts/opencode-setup.sh <v2|both|v1|check>` builds any of the three layouts [documented: the helper contract].
151: 
152: | Mode | What it does |
153: |------|--------------|
154: | `v2` (recommended) | Installs v2 to the standard prefix. Refuses when a v1 `opencode` already resolves and prints the `both` hint. |
155: | `both` (recommended) | Installs v1 and v2 into the two prefixes, links `opencode` to v2, retires `opencode2`, writes the `opencode1` launcher last, then reports both names. An `opencode2` link into the v2 prefix is removed; any other file at `opencode` or `opencode2` is moved aside to `<name>.pre-v2-default`, never deleted. |
156: | `v1` (fallback) | Installs v1 only, for users who have not updated. Refuses when a v2 `opencode` already resolves and prints the `both` hint. |
157: | `check` | Changes nothing. Reports the resolved path and the version for each name. |
158: 
159: Every mode is idempotent, and every step prints its rollback line. The helper never runs a rollback, an uninstall or an upgrade, and it changes no data file: when `opencode.db` exists and `opencode-v1.db` does not, `both` prints the copy command above instead of running it. It writes the links and the launcher only after both npm installs succeed. If the second npm install fails, the first stays installed and nothing else is written. Rerunning `both` completes the layout.
160: 
161: `check` reads the binaries from `$HOME` rather than from the caller's `PATH`, so it reports the layout even when the two disagree [documented: the helper contract].
162: 
163: ### Official v2 Channels
164: 
165: The official v2 channels as of 2026-10-18 [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/].
166: 
167: The v2 binary is named `opencode`, the same as v1's [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/], so none of these channels solves side-by-side on its own. The `opencode1` launcher is still required.
168: 
169: - `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash`
170: - `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2`
171: - `npm install -g @opencode/cli`
172: - bun, pnpm, yarn and Vite+ install paths
173: - AUR package `opencode-beta`
174: - `mise use -g opencode`. mise 2026.10.9 and later install OpenCode 2 under the name `opencode`, while older mise versions install OpenCode 1 [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/]. A mise upgrade alone can therefore move a user from v1 to v2 with no explicit choice, so pin the version when you need to stay on v1.
175: 
176: ### Homebrew Is v2-Only and Exclusive
177: 
178: `brew install opencode` installs a v2 `opencode` on the default `PATH` [confirmed: `brew info --json=v2 opencode` reports stable `2.0.32`, and the formula tracks the v2 repository].
179: 
180: There is no `opencode@1` formula and no versioned formula at all [confirmed: `versioned_formulae` is an empty list]. Homebrew therefore cannot supply the v1 leg of a side-by-side layout, and a Homebrew v2 collides with an npm v1 on the `opencode` name. One of the two becomes invisible depending on `PATH` order. Treat Homebrew as a v2-only, exclusive channel. Use it when you want only v2, and use the two-prefix npm layout when you want both.
181: 
182: ---
183: 
184: ## 4. CONFIGURATION
185: 
186: ### The Launcher
187: 
188: The launcher carries the isolation, not the packages. Its text, verbatim [confirmed: this is the file at `~/.local/bin/opencode1` on this machine, byte-identical to what the helper writes].
189: 
190: ```sh
191: #!/bin/sh
192: # OpenCode 1 fallback. OpenCode 2 owns opencode.db and migrates it in place,
193: # so v1 keeps its own copy. A relative OPENCODE_DB resolves under the shared data directory.
194: # An auto-update reinstalls the v1 package, which takes the opencode name back from v2.
195: : "${OPENCODE_DB:=opencode-v1.db}"
196: : "${OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE:=1}"
197: export OPENCODE_DB OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE
198: exec "$HOME/.local/lib/node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/opencode.exe" "$@"
199: ```
200: 
201: ### Why OPENCODE_DB Is Set
202: 
203: Both versions open `opencode.db` by default, and v2 migrates it in place [confirmed: see Layout 1]. v2 is the expected version, so it keeps the default file and v1 moves to `opencode-v1.db`. Both versions honour `OPENCODE_DB`, and a relative value resolves under the shared data directory, so `opencode-v1.db` lands beside `opencode.db` rather than in the current working directory [confirmed: on 2026-10-24 two `opencode1 run` calls added two sessions to `opencode-v1.db`, two v2 runs added two to `opencode.db`, and `opencode-v1.db` has no `session_v2` table].
204: 
205: `~/.local/share/opencode/` holds four databases on this machine [confirmed]: `opencode.db` (v2), `opencode-v1.db` (v1), `opencode-v2.db`, which holds the v2 sessions from the earlier layout and is no longer opened by either name, and `opencode-next.db`, residue from a v2 preview build. v2 imports `opencode-next.db` on its first run on a database; nothing imports `opencode-v2.db` [documented: the v2 binary's migration code reads `opencode-next.db` by name].
206: 
207: The `: "${OPENCODE_DB:=opencode-v1.db}"` form sets the variable only when it is unset or empty, so a caller can still override it for one run:
208: 
209: ```bash
210: OPENCODE_DB=/tmp/probe.db opencode1 run ...
211: ```
212: 
213: ### The Config Directory Is Shared
214: 
215: Both versions read `~/.config/opencode`, and there is no per-version config directory [confirmed: the directory holds one `opencode.jsonc`, one `plugins/` tree and one `service.json`, with no version-suffixed sibling]. A key written for one version is live on the other immediately [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/, which puts the global config at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`]. Nothing isolates them.
216: 
217: That has two consequences you cannot design around:
218: 
219: - A config key only one version understands can break the other.
220: - `~/.config/opencode` is never cleanup after uninstalling one version.
221: 
222: ### How cli-opencode Picks a Binary
223: 
224: The runtime resolves the executor in this order [documented: the cli-opencode dispatch contract].
225: 
226: 1. `$OPENCODE_BIN`, when set.
227: 2. Otherwise take `opencode2` from anywhere on `PATH`.
228: 3. Only when no `opencode2` exists anywhere on `PATH`, fall back to the first `opencode`.
229: 
230: Both halves are worth knowing. With no `OPENCODE_BIN`, the side-by-side layout has no `opencode2`, so the pick on this machine is `~/.local/bin/opencode` and a bare dispatch runs v2 [confirmed]. A v2-only layout that installs only `opencode` reaches v2 through step 3, and a v1-only machine reaches v1 the same way.

232: The rule is deliberately v2-first. OpenCode 2 is the version the repository expects and recommends; OpenCode 1 is kept only as a fallback for machines that have not updated. 240: | Working directory | No flag. The spawn directory carries it. | `--dir <path>` |
241: | Positional arguments | message text only, so every positional is a message | message text |

243: | Permission bypass | `--auto` | `--auto`, with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` as a hidden alias |
244: | Private server | `--standalone` for a dispatch that should not use the background service | not needed |

246: The v2 `run` surface on this machine is `--standalone`, `--server`, `--continue`, `--session`, `--fork`, `--model`, `--agent`, `--format`, `--file`, `--title`, `--thinking` and `--auto`, and its help lists the arguments as `message...` [confirmed: `run --help` on 2.0.32]. The v1 `run` surface adds `--dir` and `--variant`, which v2 does not have [confirmed: `run --help` on 1.19.3].
247: 
248: The `--dangerously-skip-permissions` alias is hidden from help and appears only in v1's bundled option table, where it is registered as a hidden alias of `--auto` [documented: the v1 option table]. Pass `--auto` on both versions unless a caller already pins the v1 argv.

252: The two versions list different providers, so a model id that works on one can be missing on the other [confirmed: the two lists below, read on this machine on 2026-10-18].

254: | Command | Roster-relevant providers listed |

257: | `opencode models` (1.19.3, fallback) | llmgateway-providers, llmgateway, opencode-go, openai, opencode, minimax |

259: A listing also shows any provider whose credential is still in the local auth store, including one that is off the roster. Such a provider is not a dispatch target.
260: 
261: v2 2.0.32 lists `llmgateway`, `llmgateway-providers` and `opencode`; v1 1.19.3 lists `opencode-go`, `openai` and `minimax`, which v2 2.0.32 does not [confirmed: both versions' model listings on 2026-10-18, and `opencode models --standalone` on 2026-10-20, which lists the same v2 provider prefixes]. The former OpenCode 1 default model, `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, names the `opencode-go` provider, which v2 does not list [confirmed: `opencode models` on 1.19.3], so the default on both versions is `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, which v2 does list.

263: Check the provider on the version you are about to dispatch. For a v2 run, list with `opencode models --standalone` and look for the `<provider>/` prefix: v2 `models` takes no provider argument, and without `--standalone` it asks the shared background service. For a v1 run, use `opencode1 models` side by side, or `opencode models` on a v1-only machine. Whether credentials added on one version reach the other was not probed [unknown].
264: 
265: ---
266: 
267: ## 5. VERIFICATION
268: 
269: ### Detect by Output Shape
270: 
271: ```bash
272: opencode --version    # opencode v2.1.4   -> v2 (recommended)
273: opencode1 --version   # 1.19.4            -> v1 (fallback)
274: ```
275: 
276: Both lines are observed output on this machine on 2026-10-24 [confirmed], and both match the pins.
277: 
278: Do not detect by name. A v1-only machine answers v1 to `opencode`, every other layout answers v2 to it, and only the side-by-side layout has `opencode1` [documented: the npm registry, where `@opencode/cli` declares both `opencode` and `opencode2`, so a plain v2 install also answers to `opencode2`]. Classify by what the binary prints:
279: 
280: - an `opencode v2.0.32` shape, a word before the number, is v2
281: - a bare `1.19.3` shape, digits and dots only, is v1
282: 
283: Anchor the pattern. A string like `1.19.3garbage` must not pass as v1, and the committed guard rejects it [documented: the guard's anchored pattern].
284: 
285: ### What `--version` Proves
286: 
287: `--version` proves which version a name runs. That is all it proves.
288: 
289: It does not prove that plugins load, that the config parses, that a provider is authenticated or that a dispatch will succeed. Those legs stay [unknown]. A pair that reports `1.19.3` and `opencode v2.0.32` is installed, not verified. Say "reports its version" rather than "works" until a real run has loaded a plugin on both.
290: 
291: ### What a Probe Writes
292: 
293: A v2 `--version` call is not read-only. The binary appends a `cli starting` line to `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` on every invocation, `--version` included, and `--log-level none` does not stop it, in either argument order. v1 `--version` writes nothing [confirmed: repeated probes on this machine, 2026-10-18].
294: 
295: The setup helper points `XDG_DATA_HOME` at a temporary folder for each `--version` probe and removes the folder on exit, so its probes write nothing under HOME [confirmed: a v2 probe with that variable set wrote its log line in the temporary folder, and the HOME log was unchanged, 2026-10-18]. A `--version` you run by hand still writes the log line.
296: 
297: ### Verify a Layout by Hand
298: 
299: ```bash
300: "$HOME/.local/bin/opencode" --version    # v2
301: "$HOME/.local/bin/opencode1" --version   # v1
302: ls -1 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode"/*.db
303: ```
304: 
305: ### The `check` Mode
306: 
307: `../scripts/opencode-setup.sh check` runs all of the above and changes nothing. It prints the resolved path and the reported version for `opencode`, `opencode1` and any leftover `opencode2`, which version the bare word `opencode` runs, and the database files present [documented: the helper contract].
308: 
309: ---
310: 
311: ## 6. UPGRADE
312: 
313: ### A Plain v1 Upgrade Cannot Reach 2.x
314: 
315: `opencode upgrade` with no target resolves against the `opencode-ai` channel, whose `latest` is 1.19.4, the pinned version [confirmed: `opencode upgrade --help` on 1.19.3 and the npm dist-tags on 2026-10-24]. The channel still moves by patch releases, which is why the launcher turns auto-update off and the setup helper installs the explicit pin. Nothing you do to keep v1 current can move it to 2.x except the flag below.
316: 
317: ### Never Run `opencode upgrade --major`
318: 
319: **Stop. Read the flag's own help text before you type it.**
320: 
321: ```
322: --major       upgrade to OpenCode 2 and remove OpenCode 1   [boolean]
323: ```
324: 
325: That is the complete description on 1.19.3 [confirmed]. The removal is in the flag's contract, not an implementation detail. On a side-by-side machine, `--major` migrates v1 to v2 and deletes the v1 install, which destroys the layout you built. It is a migration, never an upgrade. Do not put it in a script, a recipe or a troubleshooting step.
326: 
327: Whether it prompts for confirmation before it acts was not probed [unknown].
328: 
329: ### `upgrade --method` Is Version-Specific
330: 
331: | Method | v2 2.0.32 (recommended) | v1 1.19.3 (fallback) |
332: |--------|-------------------------|------------------------|
333: | curl, npm, pnpm, bun, brew | yes | yes |
334: | choco, scoop | no | yes |
335: | yarn, vp, winget | yes | no |
336: 
337: Both columns are read from the `--help` output on this machine [confirmed]. A shared recipe must not pass `--method`. Let each version pick its own, or build the flag per version.
338: 
339: Only the shared five are usable here, because yarn, vp and winget are absent from this machine [confirmed: `command -v`], and only npm and curl are plausible in a script.
340: 
341: ### `--log-level` Is Version-Specific Too
342: 
343: v1 accepts `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN` and `ERROR`, uppercase only [confirmed: v1 help]. v2 accepts `all`, `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `warning`, `error`, `fatal` and `none`, lowercase [confirmed: v2 help]. A shared script that passes `--log-level WARN` to v2 fails, and `--log-level warn` to v1 fails. Omit the flag, or build it per version.
344: 
345: ---
346: 
347: ## 7. UNINSTALLATION
348: 
349: ### Rollback Lines
350: 
351: The helper prints these and never runs them. Run them by hand, one layout at a time.
352: 
353: ```bash
354: # v2 leg
355: "$HOME/.local/opencode-v2/bin/opencode" uninstall --dry-run    # inspect first
356: "$HOME/.local/opencode-v2/bin/opencode" uninstall --force      # documented as keeping session data, config, state
357: npm uninstall -g --prefix "$HOME/.local/opencode-v2" @opencode/cli   # when the prefix itself goes
358: 
359: # v1 leg (fallback)
360: npm uninstall -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" opencode-ai
361: 
362: # after the v2 leg: remove ~/.local/bin/opencode, now a dangling link
363: # after the v1 leg: remove ~/.local/bin/opencode1, now a launcher with no binary
364: # after either: DO NOT delete ~/.config/opencode
365: ```
366: 
367: ### Order Matters
368: 
369: Each leg leaves names behind. Removing v2 leaves `opencode` pointing at a missing binary, and removing v1 leaves `opencode1` execing one [documented: the links' targets and the launcher's exec line]. The leftovers are harmless but confusing, and the next `check` reports names that no longer work. Whether `npm uninstall` of `opencode-ai` also removes the `opencode` link, which now points into the v2 prefix, was not probed [unknown]. Run `check` afterwards.
370: 
371: ### What v2's Uninstall Keeps
372: 
373: `opencode uninstall` is described as `Uninstall OpenCode, keeping session data, configuration, and state`, and it offers `--dry-run` to print the manifest and `--force` to skip confirmation [confirmed: `uninstall --help` on 2.0.32]. Run `--dry-run` first, read it, then `--force`.
374: 
375: On the v1 side, `npm uninstall -g --prefix ~/.local opencode-ai` removes the package. The session data in `~/.local/share/opencode/` is untouched by the npm operation [documented: the npm registry].
376: 
377: Whether the v2 background service outlives the uninstall was not probed [unknown]. Check the process list after a rollback rather than assuming either way.
378: 
379: ### Never Delete the Config Directory
380: 
381: `~/.config/opencode` is shared by both versions [documented: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/, which puts the global config at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`]. Never delete it as post-uninstall cleanup. Both versions read it, so removing it breaks whichever one remains.
382: 
383: ---
384: 
385: ## 8. TROUBLESHOOTING
386: 
387: ### Symptoms
388: 
389: | Symptom | Cause | Fix |
390: |---------|-------|-----|
391: | `opencode --version` prints `1.19.4` on a side-by-side machine | A v1 npm operation or a v1 auto-update took the `opencode` name back | Rerun `opencode-setup.sh both`, which relinks `opencode` to v2 |
392: | A v1 run opens the database v2 migrated | `OPENCODE_DB` is unset and the run bypassed the `opencode1` launcher | Run `opencode1` from `~/.local/bin`, or set `OPENCODE_DB=opencode-v1.db` yourself |
393: | A dispatch picks a version you did not expect | `$OPENCODE_BIN` is set; otherwise the first `opencode2` anywhere on `PATH` wins, and the first `opencode` is the fallback only when no `opencode2` exists | Read the resolved path, then pin `$OPENCODE_BIN` for the run |
394: | `provider/model not found` on v2 for a model that works on v1 | The provider lists differ per version | Confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix before the dispatch |
395: | `opencode1` prints `No such file or directory` and exits 126 [confirmed: a launcher whose target is missing, run on this machine] | The v1 package was uninstalled or moved | Reinstall v1, or remove the launcher |
396: | `npm` aborts with a dyld `Library not loaded` error | The node that npm runs cannot start [confirmed: Homebrew node 26.11.1 on this machine] | Put a working node earlier on `PATH` |
397: 
398: ### Gaps That No Recipe Closes
399: 
400: These constraints survive every layout. Plan around them rather than trying to fix them.
401: 
402: 1. **Homebrew cannot coexist with a v1 install.** The formula is v2-only, no versioned formula exists, and both binaries are named `opencode`.
403: 2. **`upgrade --major` is a migration that removes v1.** No recipe makes it safe on a side-by-side machine.
404: 3. **The config directory is shared.** One `~/.config/opencode` serves both versions, and a key written for one is live on the other immediately. No isolation exists to document.
405: 4. **The default database is shared.** Both versions open `opencode.db` unless `OPENCODE_DB` is set, and v2 migrates it. The `opencode1` launcher is the only thing keeping v1 off the migrated file.
406: 5. **v2's background service has no v1 analogue [confirmed: `opencode --help` lists a `service` group that `opencode --help` does not, and one service process serves the v2 clients on this machine].** Whether it outlives an uninstall was not probed [unknown].
407: 6. **`upgrade --method` and `--log-level` are version-specific.** A shared recipe must omit both.
408: 7. **bun and pnpm two-prefix behaviour is unestablished.** Only npm was verified for the two-prefix layout. Treat the other managers as single-version rather than implying parity.
409: 
410: ### Open Questions

413: |----------|--------|
414: | Does the v2 service outlive `opencode uninstall`? | [unknown] Not probed. |
415: | Do `bun add -g` and `pnpm add -g` support the two-prefix layout? | [unknown] Not probed. |
416: | Does `upgrade --major` prompt before it acts? | [unknown] Not probed. |
417: | Do the `@opencode/cli` install scripts start a service? | [unknown] Not probed. |

92: | Array order | Earlier rule wins exact ties. |

16: 
17: Structured permissions-matrix schema, resolution semantics, example matrices, RM-8 replay reasoning, and migration checklist for cli-opencode deep-loop dispatches.
18:

20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: This reference documents the structured gate schema and matching design intended to replace the RM-8 four-layer prose mitigation as the primary defense once a cli-opencode deep-loop dispatch is wired to load and enforce a permissions matrix. The design uses a flat `rules[]` array where the most-specific glob wins and first-in-array breaks exact ties.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: Read this when designing or reviewing the permissions-matrix schema, or when reasoning about how the gate is intended to block destructive scope violations once it is connected to dispatch. It does not currently gate any live `opencode run` invocation — see the status note above.
32: 
33: ### Core Principle
34: 
35: The structured gate is designed to check each tool call against deterministic `rules[]` before the tool runs, with no matching rule meaning deny. That matching logic is implemented and unit-tested, but nothing in the dispatch path calls it yet, so the matrix is not an active control for any dispatch today, configured or not.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. SCHEMA FIELDS
40: 
41: Schema file:
42: 
43: `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/assets/permissions-matrix.schema.json`
44: 
45: Examples:
46: 
47: - `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/assets/permissions-matrix.example-readonly.json`
48: - `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/assets/permissions-matrix.example-packet-local.json`
49: - `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/assets/permissions-matrix.example-repo-wide.json`
50: 
51: Top-level fields:
52: 
53: | Field | Required | Type | Meaning |
54: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
55: | `version` | yes | string | Must be `"1.0"`. |
56: | `description` | no | string | Human-readable purpose and resolution note. |
57: | `rules` | yes | array | Flat rule list evaluated by deterministic specificity. |
58: 
59: Rule fields:
60: 
61: | Field | Required | Type | Meaning |
62: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
63: | `target_glob` | yes | string | File path glob or Bash command target such as `Exec(rg)`. |
64: | `operation_class` | yes | enum | `read`, `write`, `edit`, `delete`, or `execute`. |
65: | `scope` | yes | enum | `packet-local`, `repo-wide`, or `external`. |
66: | `effect` | yes | enum | `allow` or `deny`. |
67: | `rationale` | yes | string | Audit reason surfaced in deny messages. |
68: 
69: Rule objects set `additionalProperties: false`.
70: 
71: The schema intentionally keeps the rule object small. Conditions, nested
72: allow/deny maps, and generated tokens were left out by design because the
73: schema optimizes for auditability and deterministic runtime matching.
74: 
75: ---

77: ## 3. RESOLUTION SEMANTICS
78: 
79: Runtime matching does four things.
80: 
81: 1. Normalize the tool call into an operation and one or more targets.
82: 2. Resolve file paths with `realpath` before matching.
83: 3. Filter rules by `operation_class` and `target_glob`.
84: 4. Pick the most-specific matching glob.
85: 
86: Specificity is measured as:
87: 
88: | Metric | Higher priority |
89: | --- | --- |
90: | Literal prefix length | Longer prefix wins. |
91: | Wildcards | Fewer wildcards wins. |
92: | Array order | Earlier rule wins exact ties. |
93: 
94: This means an allow rule for
95: `.opencode/specs/<track>/<packet>/**` beats a broad deny rule for
96: `**`, but two identical globs keep the first rule's effect.
97: 
98: No matching rule means deny. Empty or malformed matrix means deny.
99: 
100: ---

102: ## 4. EXAMPLE MATRIX: READ-ONLY
103: 
104: Use `permissions-matrix.example-readonly.json` for audit, review, and research
105: iterations that should not mutate the repository.
106: 
107: Core intent:

111: | `read` on `**` | allow | Review loops need corpus access. |
112: | `execute` on `Exec(rg)`, `Exec(grep)`, `Exec(git)`, `Exec(ls)`, `Exec(find)`, `Exec(cat)`, `Exec(head)`, `Exec(tail)`, `Exec(wc)`, `Exec(awk)`, `Exec(sed)` | allow | Read-only shell inspection remains ergonomic. |
113: | `execute` on `Exec(rm*)`, `Exec(mv)`, `Exec(cp)`, package managers, `node`, `python*`, and `Exec(sed -i*)` | deny | These commands can mutate files or execute mutation scripts. |
114: | `write`, `edit`, `delete` on `**` | deny | Read-only means no filesystem mutation. |

117: is wired into dispatch, it is designed to block the RM-8 class in two
118: independent ways: direct write/edit/delete tool calls deny, and the Bash
119: command targets used for deletion deny before shell execution. Today, with
120: zero production callers, neither denial path actually runs before a live tool
121: call.
122: 
123: ---

125: ## 5. EXAMPLE MATRIX: PACKET-LOCAL

135: | `write`/`edit` on the approved packet docs | allow | Packet docs are the approved continuity scope. |

137: | `edit` on `cli-opencode/SKILL.md` | allow | The packet updates only the relevant ALWAYS entry. |
138: | `execute` on read-only shell commands | allow | Search and inspection stay usable. |
139: | `execute` on destructive commands | deny | RM-8 prevention. |
140: | `write`, `edit`, `delete` on `**` | deny | Anything outside the explicit approved packet paths blocks. |
141:

143: but mutation must stay narrow.

14: # OpenCode CLI - Self-Invocation Guard (ADR-001)
15: 
16: Layered detection contract for refusing a circular cli-opencode dispatch when the calling agent is already running inside OpenCode, in both bash and python pseudocode form.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Document the full three-layer self-invocation detection contract behind ADR-001 — env-var lookup, process-ancestry probe, and state lock-file probe — so `SKILL.md` §2 (SMART ROUTING) can carry a short summary and pointer instead of the full code.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: Read this when implementing, auditing, or debugging the self-invocation guard referenced from `ROUTER.md` §3 and from `integration-patterns.md` §5 (decision tree + exact refusal message).
29: 
30: ### Core Principle
31: 
32: A running cli-opencode skill never dispatches itself. The guard trips on ANY positive detection layer unless the prompt carries explicit parallel-session keywords (use case 2 — parallel detached session), in which case the router permits a SEPARATE session id and state directory instead of a self-dispatch.
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## 2. BASH DETECTION (LAYERS 1-3)
37: 
38: ```bash
39: # Verify OpenCode CLI is available
40: command -v opencode || echo "Not installed. Run: brew install opencode (macOS) or curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash"
41: 
42: # SELF-INVOCATION GUARD (ADR-001 layered detection)
43: # Layer 1: env var lookup — any OPENCODE_* variable
44: env | grep -q '^OPENCODE_' && echo "ERROR: OPENCODE_* env detected — already inside OpenCode."
45: # Layer 2: process ancestry — opencode in parent tree
46: ps -o command= -p "$PPID" | grep -q opencode && echo "ERROR: opencode parent process detected."
47: # Layer 3: state lock-file probe
48: ls ~/.opencode/state/*/lock 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -q lock && echo "ERROR: live OpenCode session lock detected."
49: ```
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 3. PYTHON PSEUDOCODE
54: 
55: ```python
56: def detect_self_invocation():
57:     """Returns a non-None signal when the orchestrator is already running inside OpenCode."""
58:     # Layer 1: env var lookup — OpenCode sets OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR and OPENCODE_* vars
59:     for key in os.environ:
60:         if key == 'OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR' or key.startswith('OPENCODE_'):
61:             return ('env', key)
62:     # Layer 2: process ancestry — opencode in parent tree
63:     try:
64:         ancestry = subprocess.check_output(['ps', '-o', 'command=', '-p', str(os.getppid())]).decode()
65:         if '/opencode' in ancestry or 'opencode ' in ancestry:
66:             return ('ancestry', 'opencode')
67:     except subprocess.SubprocessError:
68:         pass
69:     # Layer 3: state lock-file probe
70:     state_dir = os.path.expanduser('~/.opencode/state')
71:     if os.path.isdir(state_dir):
72:         for entry in os.listdir(state_dir):
73:             if os.path.exists(os.path.join(state_dir, entry, 'lock')):
74:                 return ('lockfile', entry)
75:     return None
76: 
77: if detect_self_invocation():
78:     # Single legitimate exception: explicit "parallel detached" keywords (use case 2)
79:     # spawn a SEPARATE session id and state directory, not a self-dispatch.
80:     if not has_parallel_session_keywords(prompt):
81:         refuse(
82:             "Self-invocation refused: this agent is already running inside OpenCode. "
83:             "Use a sibling cli-* skill or a fresh shell session in a different runtime to dispatch a different model. "
84:             "For a parallel detached session, restate with explicit parallel-session keywords."
85:         )
86: ```
87: 
88: ---
89: 
90: ## 4. REFUSAL BEHAVIOR
91: 
92: When `detect_self_invocation()` returns a signal and the prompt lacks explicit parallel-session keywords, the skill refuses to load and returns the documented error message instead of generating any `opencode` invocation. See [`integration-patterns.md`](./integration-patterns.md) §5 for the full decision tree and the exact refusal text surfaced to the operator, and [`destructive-scope-violations.md`](./destructive-scope-violations.md) for the incident class this guard-plus-worktree-isolation combination protects against.
93: 
94: ---
95: 
96: ## 5. RELATED RESOURCES
97: 
98: - [`integration-patterns.md`](./integration-patterns.md) - Decision tree and exact refusal message text
99: - [`destructive-scope-violations.md`](./destructive-scope-violations.md) - RM-8 incident this guard protects against
100: - [`agent-delegation.md`](./agent-delegation.md) - Agent routing this guard gates before dispatch
101: - [`../ROUTER.md`](../ROUTER.md) - Section 3 MACHINE ROUTER, which states the guard and points here
102: - [`../SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md) - Section 4 ALWAYS rule 2

16: # OpenCode CLI - Integration Patterns
17: 
18: How cli-opencode positions itself relative to the three sibling cli-* skills, the three documented use cases (per ADR-002), the smart-router decision tree that picks between them, and the self-invocation guard that protects against circular dispatch (per ADR-001).
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: The three sibling cli-* skills exist because their target binaries are external runtimes. Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot do not own this repo. OpenCode owns this repo. A naive "delegate to opencode" skill makes no sense for an in-OpenCode operator (it would create a circular dispatch).
25: 
26: cli-opencode resolves this by documenting THREE orthogonal use cases. The smart router selects between them based on the calling AI's runtime context.
27: 
28: | Use case | Calling runtime | Target | Self-invocation? |
29: |----------|-----------------|--------|------------------|
30: | 1. External runtime to OpenCode | Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, raw shell | OpenCode for full plugin / skill / MCP runtime | No |
31: | 2. In-OpenCode parallel detached session | OpenCode itself (TUI / web / serve / acp) | New OpenCode session via `--port N` (OpenCode 1 only, no OpenCode 2 `run` form, see `./install-and-versions.md`) | No (different session id) |
32: | 3. Cross-AI orchestration handback | OpenCode / Copilot | OpenCode for spec-kit specific workflows | No |
33: 
34: The cycle ADR-001 protects against is the operator inside OpenCode asking cli-opencode to "delegate this exact prompt to OpenCode". That case is REFUSED at the routing layer.
35: 
36: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. USE CASE 1: EXTERNAL RUNTIME TO OPENCODE
41: 
42: ### When to use
43: 
44: The calling AI is Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, or a raw shell. The task needs the project's full plugin / skill / MCP runtime, not just a raw model dispatch. Examples:
45: 
46: - Run the ripgrep retrieval recipes from `system-spec-kit/references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md` against the project's spec docs
47: - Call Code Graph for semantic code search across the repo
48: - Dispatch a `@deep-research` or `@deep-review` agent loop with externalized state
49: - Run a sub-agent that needs the continuity ladder (`handover.md`, then `_memory.continuity`, then packet-first spec docs) across iterations
50: 
51: ### Smart-router signal
52: 
53: ADR-001's detection signal does NOT trip (no OPENCODE_* env var, no opencode parent process, no live state lock).
54: 
55: ### Prompt template
56: 
57: ```text
58: You are dispatching from <calling-runtime> into a fresh OpenCode session via cli-opencode.
59: 
60: Goal: <one-sentence goal>
61: 
62: Context:
63: - Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)
64: - Plugins / skills required: <list>
65: - MCP tools required: <list>
66: 
67: Constraints:
68: - <list>
69: 
70: Success criteria:
71: - <list>
72: 
73: Memory epilogue: include MEMORY_HANDBACK delimiters at the end of the response so the calling runtime can preserve context.
74: ```
75: 
76: ### Invocation shape
77: 
78: On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3):
79: 
80: ```bash
81: opencode run \
82:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
83:   --agent general \
84:   --variant max \
85:   --format json \
86:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
87:   "<prompt-from-template>" 2>&1
88: ```
89: 
90: On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the same dispatch rides `max` on the model id as `#max`, replaces `--dir` with `cd`, and adds `--standalone`:
91: 
92: ```bash
93: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run \
94:   --standalone \
95:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
96:   --agent general \
97:   --format json \
98:   "<prompt-from-template>" 2>&1
99: ```
100: 
101: On OpenCode 2.0.32, `--agent <slug>` runs the session as that agent, and an unknown slug exits 1.
102: 
103: OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider here, so a v2 reader confirms that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m` first (a 2.0.32 run used `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`).
104: 
105: ### Why it matters
106: 
107: This is the canonical cross-AI dispatch path. It gives external runtimes a one-shot bridge into the project's full runtime without forcing the operator to leave their host session.
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: ## 3. USE CASE 2: IN-OPENCODE PARALLEL DETACHED SESSION
112: 
113: ### When to use
114: 
115: The operator is already inside an OpenCode session (TUI, web, serve, acp). They want a SEPARATE OpenCode session (not a continuation, not a fork) to run an ablation suite, a worker farm, or a parallel research sweep. The new session has its own session id and its own state directory. Nothing is published: `--share` is a deprecated no-op on OpenCode 1.19.3.
116: 
117: ### Smart-router signal
118: 
119: ADR-001's detection signal trips (in-OpenCode runtime). The router checks the prompt for explicit parallel-session keywords:
120: 
121: - "parallel detached session"
122: - "ablation suite"
123: - "worker farm"
124: - "parallel research"
125: - "spawn detached"
126: - "share URL"
127: 
128: If at least one of these phrases appears AND the prompt does NOT request "delegate this exact prompt", the router permits the dispatch with `--port <N>` (OpenCode 1 only, absent on OpenCode 2 `run`, see `./install-and-versions.md`).
129: 
130: ### Prompt template
131: 
132: ```text
133: You are spawning a parallel detached OpenCode session for <purpose>.
134: 
135: Goal: <one-sentence goal>
136: 
137: Context:
138: - Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)
139: - Iteration N of <total>
140: - State file: <path>
141: 
142: Constraints:
143: - This session must NOT modify the parent session's state.
144: - Write results to <state file path>.
145: - Do not pass `--share`: it is a deprecated no-op on OpenCode 1.19.3 and publishes nothing.
146: 
147: Success criteria:
148: - <list>
149: ```
150: 
151: ### Invocation shape
152: 
153: On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3):
154: 
155: ```bash
156: opencode run \
157:   --port 4096 \
158:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
159:   --agent deep-research \
160:   --variant max \
161:   --format json \
162:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
163:   "<prompt-from-template>" 2>&1
164: ```
165: 
166: On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), `run` has no `--port`, so this shape is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32 (see `./install-and-versions.md`).
167: 
168: ### Why it matters
169: 
170: Parallel research, ablation studies, and worker farms need N concurrent sessions. Each must be independent. The detached pattern makes this possible without leaking state between sessions.
171: 
172: ### --share is a deprecated no-op
173: 
174: OpenCode 1.19.3 discontinued session sharing, so `--share` is a hidden, deprecated no-op: it prints `!  Session sharing has been discontinued` and publishes nothing. OpenCode 2 `run` has no such flag. No dispatch should pass it.
175: 
176: ---
177: 
178: ## 4. USE CASE 3: CROSS-AI ORCHESTRATION HANDBACK
179: 
180: ### When to use
181: 
182: The calling AI is a non-Anthropic CLI (OpenCode, Copilot). The task requires OpenCode-specific plugins or skills (e.g. spec-kit workflows, the project's spec folders and their continuity docs, the skill advisor). The non-Anthropic CLI cannot load the project's plugins on its own. cli-opencode is the documented bridge.
183: 
184: ### Smart-router signal
185: 
186: ADR-001's detection signal does NOT trip (the calling AI is OpenCode / Copilot, not OpenCode). The prompt mentions a project-specific subsystem:
187: 
188: - "spec kit" / "spec-kit" / "spec_kit"
189: - "spec kit memory"
190: - "code graph"
191: - "skill advisor"
192: - "session bootstrap"
193: 
194: When the calling AI is non-Anthropic AND a project-specific subsystem is named, this use case is selected over use case 1 (which is the more general path).
195: 
196: ### Prompt template
197: 
198: ```text
199: You are dispatching from <calling-runtime> into OpenCode for a spec-kit-specific workflow.
200: 
201: Goal: <one-sentence goal>
202: 
203: Context:
204: - Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)
205: - Subsystem: <spec-kit / memory / code-graph / advisor>
206: - Operation: <save / search / query / scan / validate>
207: 
208: Constraints:
209: - The OpenCode session MUST load the system-spec-kit skill for this dispatch.
210: - All MCP calls go through the project's local MCP servers.
211: 
212: Success criteria:
213: - <list>
214: 
215: Memory epilogue: include MEMORY_HANDBACK delimiters at the end so the calling runtime can preserve context.
216: ```
217: 
218: ### Invocation shape
219: 
220: On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3):
221: 
222: ```bash
223: opencode run \
224:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
225:   --agent general \
226:   --variant max \
227:   --format json \
228:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
229:   "<prompt-from-template>" 2>&1
230: ```
231: 
232: On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the same translation as use case 1 applies:
233: 
234: ```bash
235: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run \
236:   --standalone \
237:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
238:   --agent general \
239:   --format json \
240:   "<prompt-from-template>" 2>&1
241: ```
242: 
243: The invocation shape is identical to use case 1. The difference is the prompt content, which targets a project-specific subsystem.
244: 
245: ### Why it matters
246: 
247: OpenCode and Copilot cannot load this project's plugin / skill / MCP runtime on their own. cli-opencode is the documented bridge that lets a OpenCode-led orchestration call into the project's spec-kit workflows without leaving the OpenCode session.
248: 
249: ---
250: 
251: ## 5. SMART-ROUTER DECISION TREE
252: 
253: The skill's smart router picks between the three use cases (or refuses) using this decision tree:
254: 
255: ```text
256: INPUT: prompt + calling runtime
257:                 |
258:                 v
259: [ADR-001 SELF-INVOCATION GUARD]
260: - Layer 1: env var lookup (any OPENCODE_* env var present?)
261: - Layer 2: process ancestry (opencode in parent process tree?)
262: - Layer 3: best-effort lock-file probe (~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock present? -- heuristic, not guaranteed on every install)
263:                 |
264:         +-------+-------+
265:         |               |
266:        NO              YES
267:         |               |
268:         v               v
269: [CALLING RUNTIME]   [PROMPT KEYWORDS]
270:         |               |
271:    +----+----+    +-----+-----+
272:    |         |    |           |
273: Anthropic  Other  parallel   self-dispatch
274: (Claude    (OpenCode words    only
275: Code)      Copilot)        |           |
276:    |         |             v           v
277:    v         v        USE CASE 2   REFUSE
278: USE CASE  [PROJECT     (in-       (cycle —
279: 1         SUBSYSTEM    OpenCode   surface
280: (external NAMED?]      parallel)  ADR-001
281: to                      |          error)
282: OpenCode)        +------+------+
283:                  |             |
284:                 YES            NO
285:                  |             |
286:                  v             v
287:              USE CASE 3     USE CASE 1
288:              (cross-AI      (external
289:              handback)      to OpenCode)
290: ```
291: 
292: ### Refusal message
293: 
294: When the router hits the REFUSE leaf, it surfaces this exact message:
295: 
296: ```text
297: ERROR: cli-opencode self-invocation refused.
298: 
299: You are already inside OpenCode (signal: <env|ancestry|lockfile> tripped).
300: Asking cli-opencode to delegate this exact prompt back to OpenCode would create
301: a circular dispatch.
302: 
303: Options:
304: 1. Use a sibling cli-* skill (cli-claude-code, cli-opencode)
305:    to dispatch a different model.
306: 2. Open a fresh shell session (no OpenCode parent) and re-run from there.
307: 3. If you wanted a parallel detached session (different session id, separate
308:    state directory), restate the request with explicit "parallel detached" /
309:    "ablation suite" / "worker farm" / "share URL" keywords — that triggers
310:    use case 2 instead of refusal.
311: ```
312: 
313: ---
314: 
315: ## 6. STDIN HANDLING: `</dev/null` IS REQUIRED FOR ALL NON-INTERACTIVE DISPATCH
316: 
317: **On OpenCode 1, `opencode run` reads stdin at startup before session creation (opencode v1.14.39).** Without an explicit closed stdin, ANY non-interactive automation that redirects stdout/stderr hangs forever at 0% CPU, even with a clean tool registry, valid model, and `--pure` set (`--pure` is OpenCode 1 only). This is the third independent root cause discovered during the 027-xce-research-based-refinement deep-research run on 2026-05-08. See `../CHANGELOG-2026-05-08-tool-name-regex-fix.md` §Fix 4 and memory `feedback_opencode_run_requires_dev_null_stdin.md`. This stdin behaviour is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32.
318: 
319: ### Hang symptom (diagnostic)
320: 
321: If you see ALL of:
322: - Process at 0% CPU after >60s
323: - `~/.local/share/opencode/log/<timestamp>.log` last entry is `service=snapshot prune=7.days cleanup`
324: - 0 bytes stdout, 0 bytes stderr
325: - No TCP connections to provider
326: - 12-min timeout fires, exit code 124
327: 
328: …it's the stdin-startup-deadlock. Append `</dev/null`.
329: 
330: ### Failure patterns (all hang)
331: 
332: ```bash
333: # WRONG #1 — file redirect without </dev/null
334: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" > stdout.log 2> stderr.log
335: 
336: # WRONG #2 — combined redirect via tee
337: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" 2>&1 | tee combined.log
338: 
339: # WRONG #3 — background opencode in while-read loop without </dev/null
340: while IFS= read -r line; do
341:   opencode run --format json "<prompt>" > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
342: done < input.jsonl
343: # Both bugs apply: stdin-startup-read AND silent loop-stdin consumption.
344: ```
345: 
346: ### Fix patterns (all work)
347: 
348: ```bash
349: # RIGHT #1 — file redirect with </dev/null
350: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" </dev/null > stdout.log 2> stderr.log
351: 
352: # RIGHT #2 — combined redirect with explicit closed stdin via < /dev/null
353: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" </dev/null 2>&1 | tee combined.log
354: 
355: # RIGHT #3 — background in while-read loop
356: while IFS= read -r line; do
357:   opencode run --format json "<prompt>" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &
358: done < input.jsonl
359: 
360: # RIGHT #4 — foreground pipe to tail (works WITHOUT </dev/null because the empty pipe upstream provides EOF)
361: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" 2>&1 | tail -15
362: ```
363: 
364: ### Why foreground `| tail` accidentally works
365: 
366: When you run `opencode run "..." 2>&1 | tail`, the shell sets up a pipe BEFORE invoking opencode. opencode's stdin is NOT connected to your terminal. It's connected to the upstream pipe stage, which has no producer (the prompt is the positional argument, not piped via stdin). The shell closes that pipe immediately, opencode reads EOF, and startup proceeds. This is fragile. `2>&1 | tee combined.log` does NOT work because `tee` may keep the pipe open differently depending on shell + tee implementation. **Always use `</dev/null` explicitly** rather than relying on accidental pipe behavior.
367: 
368: ### Position rule
369: 
370: `</dev/null` belongs:
371: - AFTER the prompt positional argument
372: - BEFORE the `> stdout 2> stderr` redirects (or anywhere on the command line: shell parses redirects independent of position, but right-after-prompt is conventional and easiest to spot during code review)
373: 
374: ```bash
375: # canonical order
376: opencode run --flags "<prompt>" </dev/null > stdout 2> stderr
377: #                              ^^^^^^^^^^
378: #                              stdin from /dev/null (immediate EOF)
379: ```
380: 
381: ### Background dispatch from automation scripts (the deep-research / deep-review pattern)
382: 
383: On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3):
384: 
385: ```bash
386: timeout 720 opencode run \
387:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
388:   --variant max \
389:   --pure \
390:   --dangerously-skip-permissions \
391:   "$(cat prompt.md)" \
392:   </dev/null \
393:   > "$LOG_DIR/iter-N-stdout.log" \
394:   2> "$LOG_DIR/iter-N-stderr.log"
395: ```
396: 
397: On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the same dispatch adds `--standalone` and rides `max` on the model id as `#max`:
398: 
399: ```bash
400: timeout 720 opencode run \
401:   --standalone \
402:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
403:   --auto \
404:   "$(cat prompt.md)" \
405:   </dev/null \
406:   > "$LOG_DIR/iter-N-stdout.log" \
407:   2> "$LOG_DIR/iter-N-stderr.log"
408: ```
409: 
410: `--pure` (OpenCode 1 only) has no OpenCode 2 `run` form. The fanout passes `--auto` on OpenCode 2, where it approves permissions that are not explicitly denied. Whether `--auto` equals the v1-only `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is unverified (see `./install-and-versions.md`). This is the pattern enforced by the 4 `if_cli_opencode` blocks in the deep-research and deep-review YAML workflow files. Any new automation that dispatches opencode MUST follow it.
411: 
412: ### Upstream
413: 
414: The bug is in opencode v1.14.39. The fix would be: in the `run` subcommand entrypoint, check `process.stdin.isTTY` (or equivalent) and skip the stdin read in non-interactive mode. The message is already provided as a positional argument, so stdin is informational only. Until upstream patches this, `</dev/null` at every callsite is the workaround. File a bug report with opencode-ai/opencode if not already filed.
415: 
416: ---
417: 
418: ## 7. MEMORY HANDBACK
419: 
420: cli-opencode dispatches that produce evidence for a `/speckit:save` continuity write MUST include the Memory Epilogue at the end of the prompt. The dispatched session adds `MEMORY_HANDBACK_START` / `MEMORY_HANDBACK_END` delimiters around a structured JSON payload that the calling AI extracts and feeds to `generate-context.js`.
421: 
422: The full Memory Handback Protocol is shared with cli-claude-code and cli-opencode. See SKILL.md Section 4 (RULES) for the canonical 7-step procedure. The same JSON normalization (camelCase / snake_case aliases) and post-010 save gates apply.
423: 
424: ---
425: 
426: ## 8. SINGLE-DISPATCH DISCIPLINE
427: 
428: **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).** Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started: capture its PID at launch (`opencode run ... & OC_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` / `positional_scoring_fallback:app` cleanup. (A backgrounded `opencode run &` is not a process-group leader, so a group kill would miss it. Kill the captured PID directly.) **Kill only the dispatch you started, by captured PID. Never a blanket `pkill -9 -f "opencode run"` pattern (see Rule 5)**, which kills operator-owned sessions too. Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped. **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole session at start, and iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt. **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently, but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
429: 
430: ---
431: 
432: ## 9. RELATED RESOURCES

16: # OpenCode CLI - Integration Patterns
17: 
18: How cli-opencode positions itself relative to the three sibling cli-* skills, the three documented use cases (per ADR-002), the smart-router decision tree that picks between them, and the self-invocation guard that protects against circular dispatch (per ADR-001).
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: The three sibling cli-* skills exist because their target binaries are external runtimes. Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot do not own this repo. OpenCode owns this repo. A naive "delegate to opencode" skill makes no sense for an in-OpenCode operator (it would create a circular dispatch).
25: 
26: cli-opencode resolves this by documenting THREE orthogonal use cases. The smart router selects between them based on the calling AI's runtime context.
27: 
28: | Use case | Calling runtime | Target | Self-invocation? |
29: |----------|-----------------|--------|------------------|
30: | 1. External runtime to OpenCode | Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, raw shell | OpenCode for full plugin / skill / MCP runtime | No |
31: | 2. In-OpenCode parallel detached session | OpenCode itself (TUI / web / serve / acp) | New OpenCode session via `--port N` (OpenCode 1 only, no OpenCode 2 `run` form, see `./install-and-versions.md`) | No (different session id) |
32: | 3. Cross-AI orchestration handback | OpenCode / Copilot | OpenCode for spec-kit specific workflows | No |
33: 
34: The cycle ADR-001 protects against is the operator inside OpenCode asking cli-opencode to "delegate this exact prompt to OpenCode". That case is REFUSED at the routing layer.
35: 
36: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. USE CASE 1: EXTERNAL RUNTIME TO OPENCODE
41: 
42: ### When to use
43: 
44: The calling AI is Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, or a raw shell. The task needs the project's full plugin / skill / MCP runtime, not just a raw model dispatch. Examples:
45: 
46: - Run the ripgrep retrieval recipes from `system-spec-kit/references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md` against the project's spec docs
47: - Call Code Graph for semantic code search across the repo
48: - Dispatch a `@deep-research` or `@deep-review` agent loop with externalized state
49: - Run a sub-agent that needs the continuity ladder (`handover.md`, then `_memory.continuity`, then packet-first spec docs) across iterations
50: 
51: ### Smart-router signal
52: 
53: ADR-001's detection signal does NOT trip (no OPENCODE_* env var, no opencode parent process, no live state lock).
54: 
55: ### Prompt template
56: 
57: ```text
58: You are dispatching from <calling-runtime> into a fresh OpenCode session via cli-opencode.
59: 
60: Goal: <one-sentence goal>
61: 
62: Context:
63: - Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)
64: - Plugins / skills required: <list>
65: - MCP tools required: <list>
66: 
67: Constraints:
68: - <list>
69: 
70: Success criteria:
71: - <list>
72: 
73: Memory epilogue: include MEMORY_HANDBACK delimiters at the end of the response so the calling runtime can preserve context.
74: ```
75: 
76: ### Invocation shape
77: 
78: On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3):
79: 
80: ```bash
81: opencode run \
82:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
83:   --agent general \
84:   --variant max \
85:   --format json \
86:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
87:   "<prompt-from-template>" 2>&1
88: ```
89: 
90: On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the same dispatch rides `max` on the model id as `#max`, replaces `--dir` with `cd`, and adds `--standalone`:
91: 
92: ```bash
93: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run \
94:   --standalone \
95:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
96:   --agent general \
97:   --format json \
98:   "<prompt-from-template>" 2>&1
99: ```
100: 
101: On OpenCode 2.0.32, `--agent <slug>` runs the session as that agent, and an unknown slug exits 1.
102: 
103: OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider here, so a v2 reader confirms that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m` first (a 2.0.32 run used `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`).
104: 
105: ### Why it matters
106: 
107: This is the canonical cross-AI dispatch path. It gives external runtimes a one-shot bridge into the project's full runtime without forcing the operator to leave their host session.
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: ## 3. USE CASE 2: IN-OPENCODE PARALLEL DETACHED SESSION
112: 
113: ### When to use
114: 
115: The operator is already inside an OpenCode session (TUI, web, serve, acp). They want a SEPARATE OpenCode session (not a continuation, not a fork) to run an ablation suite, a worker farm, or a parallel research sweep. The new session has its own session id and its own state directory. Nothing is published: `--share` is a deprecated no-op on OpenCode 1.19.3.
116: 
117: ### Smart-router signal
118: 
119: ADR-001's detection signal trips (in-OpenCode runtime). The router checks the prompt for explicit parallel-session keywords:
120: 
121: - "parallel detached session"
122: - "ablation suite"
123: - "worker farm"
124: - "parallel research"
125: - "spawn detached"
126: - "share URL"
127:

129:

131: 
132: ```text

134: 
135: Goal: <one-sentence goal>
136: 
137: Context:
138: - Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)
139: - Iteration N of <total>
140: - State file: <path>

144: - Write results to <state file path>.
145: - Do not pass `--share`: it is a deprecated no-op on OpenCode 1.19.3 and publishes nothing.

148: - <list>
149: ```

160:   --variant max \

323: - `~/.local/share/opencode/log/<timestamp>.log` last entry is `service=snapshot prune=7.days cleanup`
324: - 0 bytes stdout, 0 bytes stderr
325: - No TCP connections to provider
326: - 12-min timeout fires, exit code 124
327: 
328: …it's the stdin-startup-deadlock. Append `</dev/null`.
329: 
330: ### Failure patterns (all hang)
331: 
332: ```bash
333: # WRONG #1 — file redirect without </dev/null
334: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" > stdout.log 2> stderr.log
335: 
336: # WRONG #2 — combined redirect via tee
337: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" 2>&1 | tee combined.log
338: 
339: # WRONG #3 — background opencode in while-read loop without </dev/null
340: while IFS= read -r line; do
341:   opencode run --format json "<prompt>" > "$LOG" 2>&1 &
342: done < input.jsonl
343: # Both bugs apply: stdin-startup-read AND silent loop-stdin consumption.
344: ```
345: 
346: ### Fix patterns (all work)
347: 
348: ```bash
349: # RIGHT #1 — file redirect with </dev/null
350: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" </dev/null > stdout.log 2> stderr.log
351: 
352: # RIGHT #2 — combined redirect with explicit closed stdin via < /dev/null
353: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" </dev/null 2>&1 | tee combined.log
354: 
355: # RIGHT #3 — background in while-read loop
356: while IFS= read -r line; do
357:   opencode run --format json "<prompt>" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &
358: done < input.jsonl
359: 
360: # RIGHT #4 — foreground pipe to tail (works WITHOUT </dev/null because the empty pipe upstream provides EOF)
361: opencode run --model X "<prompt>" 2>&1 | tail -15
362: ```
363: 
364: ### Why foreground `| tail` accidentally works
365: 
366: When you run `opencode run "..." 2>&1 | tail`, the shell sets up a pipe BEFORE invoking opencode. opencode's stdin is NOT connected to your terminal. It's connected to the upstream pipe stage, which has no producer (the prompt is the positional argument, not piped via stdin). The shell closes that pipe immediately, opencode reads EOF, and startup proceeds. This is fragile. `2>&1 | tee combined.log` does NOT work because `tee` may keep the pipe open differently depending on shell + tee implementation. **Always use `</dev/null` explicitly** rather than relying on accidental pipe behavior.
367: 
368: ### Position rule
369: 
370: `</dev/null` belongs:
371: - AFTER the prompt positional argument
372: - BEFORE the `> stdout 2> stderr` redirects (or anywhere on the command line: shell parses redirects independent of position, but right-after-prompt is conventional and easiest to spot during code review)
373: 
374: ```bash
375: # canonical order
376: opencode run --flags "<prompt>" </dev/null > stdout 2> stderr
377: #                              ^^^^^^^^^^
378: #                              stdin from /dev/null (immediate EOF)
379: ```
380: 
381: ### Background dispatch from automation scripts (the deep-research / deep-review pattern)
382: 
383: On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3):
384: 
385: ```bash
386: timeout 720 opencode run \
387:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
388:   --variant max \
389:   --pure \
390:   --dangerously-skip-permissions \
391:   "$(cat prompt.md)" \
392:   </dev/null \
393:   > "$LOG_DIR/iter-N-stdout.log" \
394:   2> "$LOG_DIR/iter-N-stderr.log"
395: ```
396: 
397: On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the same dispatch adds `--standalone` and rides `max` on the model id as `#max`:
398: 
399: ```bash
400: timeout 720 opencode run \
401:   --standalone \
402:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
403:   --auto \
404:   "$(cat prompt.md)" \
405:   </dev/null \
406:   > "$LOG_DIR/iter-N-stdout.log" \
407:   2> "$LOG_DIR/iter-N-stderr.log"
408: ```
409: 
410: `--pure` (OpenCode 1 only) has no OpenCode 2 `run` form. The fanout passes `--auto` on OpenCode 2, where it approves permissions that are not explicitly denied. Whether `--auto` equals the v1-only `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is unverified (see `./install-and-versions.md`). This is the pattern enforced by the 4 `if_cli_opencode` blocks in the deep-research and deep-review YAML workflow files. Any new automation that dispatches opencode MUST follow it.
411: 
412: ### Upstream
413: 
414: The bug is in opencode v1.14.39. The fix would be: in the `run` subcommand entrypoint, check `process.stdin.isTTY` (or equivalent) and skip the stdin read in non-interactive mode. The message is already provided as a positional argument, so stdin is informational only. Until upstream patches this, `</dev/null` at every callsite is the workaround. File a bug report with opencode-ai/opencode if not already filed.
415: 
416: ---
417: 
418: ## 7. MEMORY HANDBACK
419: 
420: cli-opencode dispatches that produce evidence for a `/speckit:save` continuity write MUST include the Memory Epilogue at the end of the prompt. The dispatched session adds `MEMORY_HANDBACK_START` / `MEMORY_HANDBACK_END` delimiters around a structured JSON payload that the calling AI extracts and feeds to `generate-context.js`.
421: 
422: The full Memory Handback Protocol is shared with cli-claude-code and cli-opencode. See SKILL.md Section 4 (RULES) for the canonical 7-step procedure. The same JSON normalization (camelCase / snake_case aliases) and post-010 save gates apply.
423: 
424: ---
425: 
426: ## 8. SINGLE-DISPATCH DISCIPLINE
427: 
428: **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).** Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started: capture its PID at launch (`opencode run ... & OC_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` / `positional_scoring_fallback:app` cleanup. (A backgrounded `opencode run &` is not a process-group leader, so a group kill would miss it. Kill the captured PID directly.) **Kill only the dispatch you started, by captured PID. Never a blanket `pkill -9 -f "opencode run"` pattern (see Rule 5)**, which kills operator-owned sessions too. Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped. **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole session at start, and iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt. **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently, but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
429: 
430: ---
431: 
432: ## 9. RELATED RESOURCES

435: - `./opencode-tools.md` - Unique value props vs sibling cli-* skills
436: - `./agent-delegation.md` - Agent routing matrix
437: - `../assets/prompt-templates.md` - Copy-paste templates per use case
438: - `../SKILL.md` - Skill entry point
439: - `../ROUTER.md` - Smart router pseudocode

39: ## 2. FULL PLUGIN, SKILL, AND MCP RUNTIME
40: 
41: ### What it does
42: 
43: When `opencode run` starts a session, the runtime loads every plugin, skill, and MCP server the project configures. The dispatched agent has access to:
44: 
45: - All `Skill` invocations the calling AI has access to (system-spec-kit, sk-doc, `sk-code` surface routing, etc.)

51: 
52: ### Why it matters
53: 
54: A Claude Code CLI dispatch via `claude -p "<prompt>"` runs raw Claude with no plugins and no MCP. To get the same plugin / skill / MCP context inside Claude Code the operator would need to run a TUI session and import the project. That is not a one-shot invocation.
55:

57:

59: 
60: ```bash
61: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3):
62: opencode run \
63:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
64:   --variant max \
65:   --format json \
66:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \

73:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
74:   --format json \
75:   "Analyze the skill-advisor daemon health using advisor_status, then propose three improvements with concrete file:line citations."
76: ```

86: ### What it does
87:

Nothing is published: `--share` is a deprecated no-op on 1.19.3, so no dispatch passes it. The original session continues unaffected.
89: 
90: ### Why it matters
91: 
92: For ablation suites, worker farms, and parallel research sweeps, the operator wants N sessions running concurrently. Each session must have:
93: 
94: - A unique session id (not a fork of the parent)
95: - An independent state directory (no shared `messages.jsonl`)
96: - The same plugin / skill / MCP runtime as the parent

98: ### Invocation shape
99: 
100: ```bash
101: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3):
102: opencode run \
103:   --port 4096 \
104:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
105:   --agent deep-research \
106:   --variant max \
107:   --format json \
108:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
109:   "Run iteration N of the deep-research loop for the approved spec folder. State file at scratch/iteration-N.jsonl."
110: ```

115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: ## 4. STRUCTURED EVENT STREAM
119: 
120: ### What it does
121: 
122: `--format json` emits a newline-delimited JSON stream with typed events: `step_start`, `tool_use`, `text` and `step_finish`. Each event carries the session id in `sessionID`, and the two versions emit the same event names.
123: 
124: ### Why it matters
125: 
126: External runtimes (Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot) parse the event stream incrementally to surface tool calls and partial messages without waiting for the full response. The schema is stable enough to write thin adapters that translate OpenCode events into the calling AI's native event format.
127: 
128: ### Invocation shape

130: ```bash

132: opencode run \
133:   --format json \
134:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
135:   --agent general \
136:   --variant max \
137:   --dir /repo \
138:   "<prompt>" 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r line; do
139:     type=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.type')
140:     case "$type" in
141:       step_start) echo "sessionID=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.sessionID')" ;;
142:       tool_use) echo "tool=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.part.tool')" ;;
143:       step_finish) echo "step_finish=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.part.reason')" ;;
144:     esac
145:   done
146: ```
147: 
148: ```bash
149: # OpenCode 2 (2.0.32):
150: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
151:   --format json \
152:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
153:   "<prompt>" 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r line; do
154:     type=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.type')
155:     case "$type" in
156:       step_start) echo "sessionID=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.sessionID')" ;;
157:       tool_use) echo "tool=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.part.tool')" ;;
158:       step_finish) echo "step_finish=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.part.reason')" ;;
159:     esac
160:   done
161: ```
